title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > How data lake tools bill: two meters
text:
Storing the files is the cheap part of a lake. You mostly pay for how much you read and how long compute runs.

Let's do the maths with published numbers only. Store 1,000 GB in S3 Standard at the first-50-TB rate of $0.023 per GB in US East (N. Virginia) and you pay $23.00 a month, before requests and transfer, per the S3 price list (checked Oct 2026).

Now query it. Athena's own pricing page shows a 3 TB table costing $15 to scan once at $5 per TB (checked Oct 2026).

After compressing the file 3 to 1 and converting it to Parquet, a query that reads one column scans 0.25 TB and costs $1.25. The page says this is a 3x saving from compression and a 4x saving from reading one column.

So file layout changes the bill, not only the vendor.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Object storage
text:
**1. Amazon S3: best for the default object store on AWS**

At a glance

- Layer: object storage
- Price: S3 Standard $0.023 per GB a month for the first 50 TB, then $0.022 and $0.021 at higher volumes, in US East (N. Virginia), per Amazon's S3 price list (checked Oct 2026)

Amazon's S3 pricing page says your rate depends on the size of your objects, how long you store them and the storage class. It also lists S3 Tables, which store Apache Iceberg tables and carry their own storage, request and monitoring charges (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- The same price list shows lower-priced classes such as Standard-Infrequent Access at $0.0125 per GB-month in US East (N. Virginia) (checked Oct 2026).
- The S3 user guide says S3 gives strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE requests in all AWS Regions, and that an update to a single key is atomic.
- A single object can be up to 50 TB when you use the multipart upload API, and one PUT can carry an object up to 5 GB, per the AWS upload docs (checked Oct 2026).
- The same price list gives S3 Standard request rates in US East (N. Virginia): $0.005 per 1,000 PUT, COPY, POST or LIST requests and $0.0004 per 1,000 GET requests (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- It stores files, and that's it. Without a table format and an engine, you get no tables.
- The same user guide says "There is no way to make atomic updates across keys," so S3 alone cannot commit a change to many files at once (checked Oct 2026). Table formats such as Iceberg (entry 4) add that with an atomic metadata swap.
- Requests and data transfer are billed on top, and the first 100 GB a month of transfer out is free only in aggregate across AWS. The pricing page says request costs depend on the request type and are charged on the quantity of requests (checked Oct 2026).
- S3 Tables, the Iceberg option on the same page, bills an object monitoring fee per object stored in table buckets on top of storage and requests (checked Oct 2026).
- The largest file the S3 console can upload is 160 GB, so very large objects go through the multipart upload API, per the AWS upload docs (checked Oct 2026).

**2. Azure Data Lake Storage: best for Microsoft shops that want folder-style storage**

At a glance

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Object storage (part 2)
text:
- Layer: object storage
- Price: priced at Azure Blob Storage levels, per Microsoft's overview (page updated July 3, 2026), with rates by tier and operation on the Azure pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

Microsoft's overview calls it a set of capabilities built on Azure Blob Storage, switched on by the hierarchical namespace setting. In other words, it isn't a separate service or account type.

What's good

- Microsoft's overview says renaming or deleting a folder is one atomic operation (all or nothing), which it presents as a fit for big analytics jobs. We did not test that.
- Access control supports both Azure role-based access control (RBAC) and POSIX access control lists (ACLs), set at the directory or file level (same overview).
- The overview says all data is encrypted at rest, with either Microsoft-managed or customer-managed keys.
- Microsoft says individual files can run from a few KB to hundreds of TB, with no limits on account size, file size or total data (checked Oct 2026).
- Hadoop distributions include the Azure Blob File System (ABFS) driver, and Microsoft names Apache Spark and Presto as engines that read the data through it.

Where it falls short

- Most Blob Storage features work, but Microsoft says some are preview only and a handful aren't supported (checked Oct 2026).
- The overview page says nothing about Iceberg, so check your engine's docs.
- Turning on the hierarchical namespace cannot be undone. Microsoft's upgrade guide says "There's no way to revert your account once you've performed the upgrade." (checked Oct 2026)
- On the Azure pricing page, the hierarchical namespace adds a charge for the extra metadata that holds the folder structure, shown as an Index meter. Data in Cool, Cold and Archive also carries early deletion periods of 30, 90 and 180 days, and the charge is prorated (checked Oct 2026).
- The same page prices operations in 4 MB units: in the East US hierarchical view, Hot-tier writes list at $0.065 and reads at $0.0052 per 10,000 operations, and Archive reads at $6.50 (checked Oct 2026).
- The same page lists data retrieval at $0.01 per GB for Cool, $0.03 for Cold and $0.02 for Archive, with Hot free, so reading back from the colder tiers is a separate charge (checked Oct 2026).

**3. Google Cloud Storage: best for lakes on Google Cloud with a free starter allowance**

At a glance

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Object storage (part 3)
text:
- Layer: object storage
- Price: set per location and storage class; Always Free includes 5 GB-months of Standard storage, counted across US-WEST1, US-CENTRAL1 and US-EAST1, per the Google Cloud Storage pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

The pricing page lists Standard, Nearline, Coldline and Archive classes, plus a Rapid storage class. Look at the retrieval table, which shows $0 per gibibyte (GiB) for Standard, $0.01 for Nearline, $0.02 for Coldline and $0.05 for Archive (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- The retrieval table lists $0 per GiB for Standard storage, and the Always Free allowance is 5 GB-months (checked Oct 2026).
- Always Free also includes 5,000 Class A operations and 50,000 Class B operations a month, plus 100 GB of data transfer from North America to each Google Cloud data transfer destination (checked Oct 2026).
- Retrieval fees do not apply to objects in a bucket with Autoclass enabled, per the pricing page (checked Oct 2026).
- The retrieval table lists $0 per GiB for the Rapid class too (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Storage prices change by location and are shown per hour, so there's no single number to quote (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page doesn't state Iceberg support. Google's Iceberg tables live in the BigQuery entry below.
- Data processing costs include operation charges for all requests, retrieval fees for reading data in some storage classes, and inter-region replication charges for data written to dual-regions and multi-regions (checked Oct 2026).
- Autoclass charges, Storage Intelligence charges and charges for objects with attached contextual information (Objects Contexts) are billed as data processing costs too (checked Oct 2026).
- The Always Free quotas apply only to usage in US-WEST1, US-CENTRAL1 and US-EAST1, are counted across those three regions together, and do not apply to the Rapid class (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Open Table Formats
text:
**4. Apache Iceberg: best for one table format many engines can read**

At a glance

- Layer: table format
- Price: free, Apache 2.0 licence (checked Oct 2026)

Iceberg's maintenance docs say each write creates a new snapshot, snapshots pile up until you expire them, and streaming jobs can leave many small files that need compaction. The specification says versions 1, 2 and 3 are complete, and version 4 is still in development (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Trino, Athena, Databricks and Snowflake all document Iceberg support, as the entries below show.
- The specification says version 2 adds delete files, so single rows can be deleted or replaced in immutable data files without rewriting those files.
- Version 3 adds row lineage tracking and binary deletion vectors, per the same specification.
- Table state lives in metadata files, and each change swaps in a new metadata file atomically. The specification also lists readers that take no locks as a design goal.
- Maintenance tools ship with the project: the maintenance page describes an expireSnapshots operation, a Spark rewriteDataFiles action that combines small files in parallel, and a deleteOrphanFiles action.

Where it falls short

- It's only a format. You still need storage, a catalog and an engine.
- Upkeep is your job (or your platform's): compaction, snapshot expiry and cleaning of orphan files.
- Snapshots accumulate until they are expired, and expiring a snapshot removes it from time travel queries.
- Small data files add metadata and slow queries, and the maintenance page says streaming queries may produce small files that need compaction (checked Oct 2026).
- Old metadata files are kept by default, per the maintenance page, and tables with frequent commits, such as those written by streaming jobs, may need regular metadata cleanup.
- Engine support differs by version: the Athena entry below creates only v2 tables, Trino lists v3 as experimental, and Snowflake's docs say row-level equality deletes are not supported (checked Oct 2026).

**5. Delta Lake: best for teams already on Databricks or Fabric**

At a glance

- Layer: table format
- Price: free, Apache 2.0 licence, per delta-io/delta on GitHub (checked Oct 2026)

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Open Table Formats (part 2)
text:
Delta Lake's site calls it an open-source storage framework for a lakehouse and says no single company controls it, with oversight from the Linux Foundation. It lists Spark, Flink, Trino, Hive, Snowflake, BigQuery, Athena, Redshift and Databricks among supported engines.

What's good

- Delta's UniForm page says Delta Universal Format, called UniForm, lets Iceberg and Hudi clients read Delta tables. It labels the Hudi part a preview.
- Delta's home page lists ACID transactions (serializability, the strongest isolation level) and scalable metadata for petabyte-scale tables as key features.
- Delta's site says it is platform agnostic: use it with any query engine, on any cloud, on-premises or locally.
- Delta's site says the project has more than 190 developers from over 70 organizations and is used in over 10,000 production environments. Both figures are the project's own and undated.

Where it falls short

- The UniForm page says UniForm generates its Iceberg metadata asynchronously and is read-only from an Iceberg and Hudi perspective (checked Oct 2026).
- UniForm does not work on tables with deletion vectors enabled, and you run REORG when enabling UniForm Iceberg on such a table (checked Oct 2026).
- The same page says that if an external writer (not Delta Lake) writes to a UniForm Iceberg or Hudi table, it may destroy the Delta table and cause data loss (checked Oct 2026).
- Change Data Feed and Delta Sharing work for Delta clients when UniForm is on, but have no support in Iceberg (checked Oct 2026).
- Microsoft Fabric stores its tables in Delta Parquet, so Delta is the home format there and Iceberg is a bridge (checked Oct 2026).

**6. Apache Hudi: best for tables that take frequent updates and deletes**

At a glance

- Layer: table format
- Price: free, Apache 2.0 licence, per Hudi's docs overview (checked Oct 2026)

Hudi's overview calls it an open table format built for high-performance writes on incremental data pipelines. It lists upserts (an update or an insert in one step), deletes, indexes, clustering, compaction and concurrency control, and two table types, copy-on-write and merge-on-read.

What's good

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Open Table Formats (part 3)
text:
- The overview lists Spark, Flink, Presto, Trino and Hive as query engines.
- The overview lists three query types: Snapshot Queries, Incremental Queries and Read-Optimized Queries.
- The overview says Hudi-rs is a native Rust implementation of Hudi that also provides bindings to Python, for use outside the JVM.
- The overview names Uber, Amazon, ByteDance and Robinhood among those transforming their production data lakes with Hudi. That is Hudi's own list and we did not check it.
- The overview offers quick start guides for Spark, Flink and Python/Rust, and a Docker demo that runs Hudi with Kafka, Spark, Hive and Presto.

Where it falls short

- The overview doesn't state Iceberg compatibility, so confirm your engine reads Hudi before you commit.
- Cross-table interoperability between Hudi, Delta Lake and Iceberg is the job of Apache XTable, which says it is incubating in the Apache Software Foundation and was recently renamed from OneTable.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Query engines
text:
**7. Trino: best for open-source SQL across many sources**

At a glance

- Layer: query engine
- Price: open source, with the Apache 2.0 licence listed in Trino's GitHub repository; no vendor price is listed (checked Oct 2026)

Trino's Iceberg connector page says it supports Iceberg spec versions 1 and 2, with version 3 experimental (checked Oct 2026). It reads Parquet, Optimized Row Columnar (ORC) and Avro files, and works with catalogs such as Hive Metastore and AWS Glue.

What's good

- Its docs list INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and MERGE on Iceberg tables, so it isn't read-only. We did not test them.
- The connector page lists these catalogs: Hive Metastore, AWS Glue, JDBC, REST, Nessie and Snowflake.
- New tables can use Iceberg format version 1, 2 or 3 and default to 2, and the connector supports CREATE TABLE AS with SELECT syntax, per the connector page (checked Oct 2026).
- The table_changes function reads row-level changes between two versions (snapshots) of an Iceberg table.

Where it falls short

- It is a query engine only. Trino's overview describes a distributed SQL query engine for data held in other sources, and the docs we read describe software you run yourself, with no hosted service (checked Oct 2026).
- Version 2 is required for row-level deletes, and the docs say version 3 support is experimental: row-level updates, deletes and OPTIMIZE are not supported on v3 tables (checked Oct 2026).
- Tables with v3 features such as column default values and encryption are not supported, and the docs say writing to encrypted tables is not supported (checked Oct 2026).
- The table_changes function does not support tables with delete files, which row-level operations typically produce (checked Oct 2026).

**8. Amazon Athena: best for occasional SQL over files in S3**

At a glance

- Layer: query engine
- Price: $5.00 per TB of data scanned in US East (Ohio), per AWS's Athena price list (checked Oct 2026)

Athena's Iceberg docs say it can read, write, run table-changing commands called data definition language (DDL) and time-travel on Iceberg tables. The same price list adds a catch: it applies a 10 MB minimum to each successful or canceled query (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Query engines (part 2)
text:
- AWS positions it as serverless, so there are no servers to run, and it bills per query.
- The Athena pricing page says you can use SQL or Apache Spark with no infrastructure to set up or manage, and that Athena queries data directly in Amazon S3 with no additional storage charges for querying (checked Oct 2026).
- The price list shows DDL statements, failed queries and statements that create or load partitions as free query types (checked Oct 2026).
- Beyond per-TB billing, the pricing page's examples price Capacity Reservations at $0.30 per DPU-hour and Spark at $0.35 per DPU-hour (checked Oct 2026).
- Athena engine version 3 supports the Iceberg file formats Parquet, ORC and Avro, per the Athena Iceberg docs (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- The docs list Iceberg version 1.4.2 and say Athena creates and operates only on Iceberg v2 tables (checked Oct 2026).
- Only tables created against the AWS Glue catalog work. Athena supports Glue optimistic locking only, and the docs warn that modifying an Iceberg table with any other lock implementation will cause potential data loss and break transactions (checked Oct 2026).
- Timestamps keep millisecond precision in reads and writes, although Iceberg supports microsecond precision (Athena Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- DDL isn't supported on Iceberg tables registered with Lake Formation (Athena Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- The docs say Athena does not support ALTER TABLE SET LOCATION on Iceberg tables, or partitioning them by nested fields (checked Oct 2026).
- If you use the AWS Glue Data Catalog with Athena, you are charged standard Data Catalog rates on top of the query price, per the pricing page (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Governance
text:
**9. AWS Lake Formation: best for fine-grained access rules on AWS lakes**

At a glance

- Layer: governance and catalog
- Price: permissions and their use by integrated services are at no charge; underlying services bill normally, per the Lake Formation pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

The Lake Formation docs say it manages access to data on S3 and its metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Its rules can apply at database, table, column, row and cell level, and are enforced across AWS services such as Athena and AWS Glue.

What's good

- AWS documents tag-based access control, so rules can be set by label rather than table by table. We did not test how well that scales. The docs say the tags (LF-Tags) attach to databases, tables or columns.
- The docs say permissions are enforced with column, row and cell-level controls across Amazon Athena, Amazon Quick, Amazon Redshift Spectrum, Amazon EMR and AWS Glue.
- Lake Formation provides audit logs through CloudTrail to monitor access.
- It can import data from MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MariaDB and Oracle databases running in Amazon RDS or hosted on Amazon EC2, and the docs say both bulk and incremental loading are supported.
- Amazon S3 Tables can be published and cataloged as Data Catalog objects, with the catalog registered as a Lake Formation data location.

Where it falls short

- It governs data but doesn't store or query it. The Lake Formation pricing page also says the Storage API, Governed Tables and the Storage Optimizer bill separately (checked Oct 2026).
- The Storage API is charged for bytes scanned, rounded up to the next megabyte with a 10 MB minimum, and Governed Tables are charged for the number of files tracked plus API calls that read or change that metadata, per the same pricing page (checked Oct 2026).
- It's an AWS tool, and as the Athena entry above shows, there's a limit on Iceberg tables registered with it.
- Athena's docs say Lake Formation can manage read access for Iceberg, Hudi and Delta Lake tables, but not permissions for VACUUM, MERGE, UPDATE or OPTIMIZE on them (checked Oct 2026).
- For databases other than the five it lists, the docs say to create custom ETL jobs with AWS Glue.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Ingestion
text:
**10. OLake Go: best for getting database changes into an Iceberg lake**

At a glance

- Layer: ingestion
- Price: free, Apache 2.0 licence (OLake on GitHub) (checked Oct 2026); you run it on your own servers
- Support: contact the OLake team

A lake stays empty until something loads it. OLake Go is an open-source tool that copies database tables into Apache Iceberg tables in storage you choose or into Parquet files. It captures changes from PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server.

What's good

- It has four sync modes, Full Refresh, Full Refresh + Incremental, Full Refresh + CDC and CDC Only, so one tool does the first load and then keeps the copy current (docs).
- Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka also work as sources, without database change capture.
- It writes Iceberg tables to catalogs such as AWS Glue, with eleven catalog types listed on the catalog compatibility page, so engines such as Trino can read them (see the compatibility page for catalogs per engine).
- Syncs are stateful and resumable: after a crash, a network failure or a pause they resume from the last checkpoint instead of starting over (docs).
- Schema discovery runs at the start of every sync, and a new source column is added to the Iceberg schema automatically (schema evolution docs).
- You run it yourself with Docker, Helm on Kubernetes or the OLake UI.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms
text:
**11. Databricks: best for Spark, SQL and machine learning in one workspace**

At a glance

- Layer: platform
- Price: pay as you go, billed in Databricks Units (DBUs); on the Premium plan on AWS US East, SQL Serverless was $0.70, SQL Pro $0.55 and SQL Classic $0.22 per DBU, per the Databricks SQL pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

Databricks' Iceberg docs say it supports Iceberg tables in Parquet, using versions 1, 2 and 3 of the specification, with Unity Catalog managing the tables (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Its docs say it supports managed Iceberg tables and can read other catalogs such as AWS Glue and Snowflake Horizon.
- Managed Iceberg tables can be created with Databricks Runtime, Databricks SQL, or external Iceberg-compatible engines that support the Iceberg REST Catalog API (Iceberg docs).
- Databricks' external access page says the Iceberg REST catalog lets clients such as Apache Spark, Apache Flink and Trino read from and write to Unity Catalog Iceberg tables.
- Serverless SQL warehouses typically start in 2 to 6 seconds, per the Databricks warehouse types page (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Managed Iceberg tables need Unity Catalog, Databricks Runtime 16.4 LTS or newer, and serverless compute, and that serverless compute must have network connectivity to the storage account behind the table (Databricks Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Foreign Iceberg tables, the ones managed in another catalog, are read-only in Databricks and have limited platform support (Databricks Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Through the REST catalog, external Iceberg clients can't access views and can't run table maintenance such as expiring snapshots and removing orphan files, per the external access page (checked Oct 2026).
- Partition evolution on managed Iceberg tables works through external Iceberg engines using the REST catalog, but not through Databricks SQL (Databricks Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Pro and Classic SQL warehouses take typically about 4 minutes to start, and a Classic warehouse's compute runs in your own AWS account, per the warehouse types page (checked Oct 2026).
- The per-DBU price may not be the full bill. The pricing page says SQL Serverless includes cloud instance cost, but the Classic and Pro cards describe self-managed warehouses and carry no such note, so check cloud charges (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms (part 2)
text:
**12. Snowflake: best for SQL teams that want Iceberg on storage they control**

At a glance

- Layer: platform
- Price: credits; on-demand $2.00 per credit on Standard, AWS US East, per the Snowflake Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026), effective October 15, 2026

Snowflake's Iceberg docs say Iceberg tables combine Snowflake's performance with external cloud storage that you manage. It supports Parquet files, and writes to externally managed tables through a remote Iceberg catalog that uses the Representational State Transfer (REST) interface. Row-level deletes use position deletes on v2 tables and deletion vectors on v3 tables (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Per its docs, you can use Snowflake as the catalog, or an external catalog such as AWS Glue or Snowflake Open Catalog.
- The docs say your files stay in storage you manage.
- An Iceberg table that uses Snowflake as its catalog gets full Snowflake platform support with read and write access.
- Snowflake's externally managed writes page says it can run INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, TRUNCATE TABLE and COPY INTO on externally managed Iceberg tables.
- The credit table lists a Standard warehouse at 1 credit an hour for X-Small, 2 for Small and 4 for Medium, doubling at each size up to 512 for 6XL, per the Snowflake credit table (checked Oct 2026), effective October 15, 2026.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms (part 3)
text:
- If your account and storage sit in different regions, the docs say egress costs apply when you query, and Snowflake bills cross-region transfer for its managed Iceberg tables (checked Oct 2026).
- It's a proprietary managed service, and we found no self-hosted option on the pages read. Credit prices vary by edition and region, so $2.00 is one row in a table, not a promise: the same table lists Enterprise at $3.00 in AWS US East and Standard in AWS EU Frankfurt at $2.60 (checked Oct 2026).
- An Iceberg table that uses an external catalog "provides limited Snowflake platform support", and the docs say row-level deletes with equality delete files aren't supported (checked Oct 2026).
- Writes to externally managed tables allow autocommit transactions only (no multi-statement transactions), and CREATE ICEBERG TABLE ... AS SELECT isn't supported when the remote catalog is AWS Glue or Databricks Unity Catalog, per the externally managed writes page (checked Oct 2026).
- For the AWS Glue Data Catalog, dropping an externally managed table through Snowflake does not delete the underlying table files, per the same page (checked Oct 2026).
- For Iceberg tables created from Iceberg metadata files in object storage, the docs say Snowflake does not assume any life-cycle management on the table (checked Oct 2026).

**13. Dremio: best for self-service SQL on Iceberg, with a self-managed choice**

At a glance

- Layer: platform
- Price: Dremio Cloud $0.20 per Dremio Compute Unit (DCU); Dremio Enterprise is Contact Sales, per the Dremio pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

The pricing page (checked Oct 2026) calls Cloud a fully managed lakehouse on AWS, with Azure coming soon, and claims zero infrastructure and automatic scaling and optimization. We did not test those claims. Enterprise is self-managed on cloud, Kubernetes, on-prem or Dremio-as-a-Service.

What's good

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms (part 4)
text:
- The pricing page (checked Oct 2026) says Dremio Cloud includes a 30-day free trial with $400 in credits, and that the trial needs no credit card.
- The same page lists a Dremio Community Edition, a free query engine for local machines or servers (checked Oct 2026).
- Dremio's Iceberg docs say Iceberg is supported in Dremio v21.0 and later, and that connected sources use default Iceberg catalogs that support both read and write commands.
- The same docs say the built-in Iceberg catalog is based on Apache Polaris (incubating) and gives read and write access to Iceberg tables across REST-compatible query engines.

Where it falls short

- Dremio Cloud runs on AWS only for now, with Azure listed as coming soon on its pricing page (checked Oct 2026).
- The Enterprise price isn't published on the pricing page, which says to contact sales (checked Oct 2026).
- Dremio's Iceberg docs say "Only Parquet file formats are currently supported" for Iceberg tables, and that Amazon DynamoDB and JDBC catalogs are not supported (checked Oct 2026).
- The same docs say Dremio does not support reading global equality deletes for Apache Iceberg v2 tables in the case they describe, where the delete file's partition spec is unpartitioned (checked Oct 2026).

**14. Microsoft Fabric OneLake: best for Microsoft teams that want one lake**

At a glance

- Layer: platform and storage
- Price: each workspace sits in a capacity billed separately; rate not read, per Microsoft's OneLake overview (checked Oct 2026) (updated August 23, 2026)

Microsoft's OneLake overview says every Fabric tenant includes one OneLake, built on Azure Data Lake Storage. It stores tables in Delta Parquet or Iceberg format.

What's good

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms (part 5)
text:
- Microsoft says shortcuts point to data in S3, Azure storage and Iceberg sources without copying it.
- Its docs say metadata virtualization lets Iceberg tables be read as Delta in Fabric, and Delta tables be read by external Iceberg readers.
- You can write Iceberg tables directly to OneLake or create shortcuts to Iceberg tables stored externally (OneLake Iceberg page (checked Oct 2026)).
- OneLake supports Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 APIs and SDKs, so existing ADLS Gen2 applications can be used (overview (checked Oct 2026)).
- The overview says database mirroring continuously replicates data from an operational database into OneLake as analytics-ready Delta tables.
- Business users can build Power BI reports on top of OneLake by using Direct Lake mode in the Analysis Services engine (overview (checked Oct 2026)).

Where it falls short

- The docs say Fabric engines store data in Delta Parquet, so Iceberg is bridged rather than the default.
- The tenant gets a single OneLake instance, and Microsoft says you can't delete OneLake or create multiple OneLakes (checked Oct 2026).
- Microsoft's table format conversion page says conversion supports Parquet only, in both directions, and that source tables must have fewer than 5,000 transactions or commits (checked Oct 2026).
- On that page, Iceberg V2 source tables are supported but V3 is partially supported, and Iceberg equality deletes cause conversion to fail (checked Oct 2026).
- Generating the converted metadata can take between 5 seconds and 2 minutes, and conversion isn't supported for tenants or workspaces with private links enabled (same page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Each workspace sits in a capacity that is tied to a region and billed separately, and the overview gives no rates (checked Oct 2026).

**15. Google BigQuery: best for SQL teams on Google Cloud who want Iceberg tables in their own buckets**

At a glance

- Layer: platform
- Price: on-demand queries $6.25 per TiB after the first 1 TiB a month, shown for Iowa (us-central1); capacity pricing in slots is also offered, per the BigQuery pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

Google's Iceberg docs call them Apache Iceberg managed tables, formerly BigLake tables for Apache Iceberg in BigQuery. The docs say they keep data in customer-owned storage buckets and support Iceberg V2, with the same managed experience as standard BigQuery tables (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > The 15 best data lake tools > Platforms (part 6)
text:
What's good

- Table changes run in GoogleSQL data manipulation language.
- The docs say BigQuery can export an Iceberg V2 snapshot, refreshed on each table change if you turn on metadata auto-refresh, so open-source engines such as Spark can read the table.
- Iceberg managed tables get automatic storage optimization: adaptive file sizing, automatic clustering, garbage collection and metadata optimization (Iceberg managed tables docs).
- Schema evolution covers adding, dropping and renaming columns and changing an existing column's data type and mode (same page).
- The pricing page says the first 1 TiB of query data processed per month is free, the first 10 GiB of storage is free each month, and storage not modified for 90 consecutive days drops in price by approximately 50% (checked Oct 2026).
- Standard edition slots list at $0.04 per hour with no commitment, billed per second with a one-minute minimum, per the pricing page (the price varies by region and edition) (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- The docs say only one mutating statement (UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE) runs on a table at a time, so the rest queue up (checked Oct 2026).
- Renaming, copying and cloning these tables aren't supported, and neither are table snapshots (CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE), per the Iceberg managed tables docs (checked Oct 2026).
- On-demand queries are billed for the data processed in the columns you select, even if you set an explicit LIMIT, with a 10 MB minimum per table referenced and per query, per the pricing page (checked Oct 2026).
- On-demand pricing generally gives access to up to 2,000 concurrent slots, shared among all queries in a project, per the pricing page (checked Oct 2026).
- The editions page says Standard edition has no column-level access control, row-level security or data masking, no BigQuery ML, no VPC Service Controls and no capacity commitments (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > How to choose data lake tools
text:
Don't start with brand names. Start from the cloud you already pay for and the skills on your team, then ask where you want to be free to switch.

| If this is true | Start with | Why | Watch out for |
| You are on AWS and want pay-per-query | S3 plus Athena, add Lake Formation for access rules | Nothing to run | Iceberg v2 only, Glue catalog only |
| You are on Azure and use Power BI | ADLS or Fabric OneLake | One lake, one identity system | Delta is the home format |
| You have engineers and want no platform fee | Object storage, Iceberg and Trino | Open parts, free software | Engine setup and upkeep are yours |
| You want one vendor for Spark and machine learning | Databricks | Many workloads in one place | Unity Catalog needed for managed Iceberg |
| Your team writes SQL and wants a managed engine | Snowflake, BigQuery or Dremio Cloud | Little to operate | Egress charges, BigQuery's limit of one mutating statement per table, or Dremio Enterprise (self-managed) with no published price |
| Your data starts in Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server | OLake Go | Open source, copies database tables into Iceberg tables | Pair it with a catalog and an engine from the entries above |
| Your tables get many updates | Hudi or Iceberg, check engine support | Built for row-level changes | Table upkeep is yours |

The short read: with engineers to spare, the open parts give you the most room to move. Without them, a pay-per-query service or a bundled platform means less to look after.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > How to choose data lake tools > Which data lake setup fits you?
text:
Question 1 of 6

Which cloud do you already pay for?

Moving data across clouds or regions adds transfer charges.

Six questions to ask before you buy
- Which cloud do you already pay for? Moving data across clouds or regions adds transfer charges.
- Which table format does your engine write? "Supports Iceberg" can mean read only.
- Who does the upkeep? Compaction and snapshot expiry are yours unless a platform does them.
- Which meter do you pay? Bytes scanned, compute units or flat capacity.
- Who needs row or column rules? Price a governance layer early, not at the end.
- How will data get in? The tools above store, organize and query data. Loading your databases into the lake is a separate job (entry 10).

Ask any vendor for a worked bill on your own data volume. Claims such as the automatic scaling that Dremio's pricing page describes are the vendor's own words.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > So where does that leave you?
text: Choose layers first and brand names second. A cloud object store, an open table format and one engine cover many teams, while Databricks, Snowflake, Dremio and Fabric trade some choice for less upkeep. Whichever you pick, store data in Parquet and an open table format: file layout cuts the bill, and open formats ease an exit, though engine support differs.

title: Compare: Best Data Lake Tools in 2026, by Layer | OLake > FAQs
text:
Q1. What are data lake tools?

The pieces you stack to build a data lake: object storage, a table format, a query engine and a governance layer. Some vendors sell several layers together as a platform.

Q2. Is Amazon S3 a data lake?

Not on its own. S3 is storage, and S3 Tables adds Apache Iceberg tables. You still choose an engine and a way to control access.

Q3. Do I need Iceberg, Delta Lake or Hudi?

You can store raw files without one, but you give up row-level updates and version rollback. Check which format your main engine supports first, and let that decide.

Q4. How much does a data lake cost?

It depends on how much you store and how much you read. 1,000 GB in S3 Standard at $0.023 per GB (US East, N. Virginia) is $23.00 a month before requests (S3 price list), and Athena bills $5.00 per TB scanned (US East, Ohio) (Athena price list). Platforms bill compute units instead (checked Oct 2026).

Q5. What is the difference between a data lake and a lakehouse?

A lakehouse is a lake with a table format and engine that give it database-like behavior, such as row-level updates and earlier versions of a table.

Q6. How do I load data from my databases into a lake?

You need a loading tool that copies tables or database changes into lake files. Entry 10 above covers one open-source option, OLake Go.

Q7. Which data lake tool is cheapest?

Storage is the cheap layer: S3 Standard lists $0.023 per GB a month in US East (N. Virginia) (S3 price list). After that the meter decides: Athena bills $5.00 per TB scanned (US East, Ohio) (Athena price list) and BigQuery on-demand $6.25 per TiB after the first free TiB (Iowa) (BigQuery pricing) (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake
text:
Key takeaways

The best data management platform depends on the job, because no single product does all of it. Fivetran, Airbyte and OLake Go move your data. Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks store and query it, while Microsoft Purview, Collibra, OpenMetadata and DataHub catalog and govern it.

Great Expectations checks quality, and Informatica and Semarchy manage master data, the single trusted record of a customer or product. So start with the pain you have today: data that's hard to reach, or data nobody trusts.

- "Data management platform" has two meanings. In advertising it means a tool that builds audience groups for ad targeting. This guide is about the other one: tools that move, store, catalog, check and govern your company's own data.
- No tool covers everything. The Data Management Body of Knowledge (DMBOK), a widely used reference, lists 11 areas of data management. We found no vendor page claiming all 11.
- Price information hides in different places.Collibra and Semarchy publish no price, and Informatica shows no dollar rate on its pricing page. Fivetran, Airbyte, BigQuery and Databricks at least publish their billing units, and Fivetran prints its per-row list rates in a separate Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026).
- Open source covers the catalog and quality jobs.OpenMetadata, DataHub and Great Expectations are all Apache-2.0 licensed on GitHub (checked Oct 2026). The catch: you run them yourself, unless you buy a managed route such as DataHub Cloud.

We checked prices and plans against each vendor's own pages in October 2026, and each price, plan and limit below carries its link and a `(checked Oct 2026)` note. Plans change often, so confirm on the vendor's page before you buy.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > What is a data management platform?
text:
Data management means looking after data from the day it's created until the day it's deleted.

The Data Management Body of Knowledge (DMBOK), a reference framework from a professional body for data managers, lists 11 areas. They include governance, architecture, security, integration, master data, metadata and data quality.

A data management platform is software that covers some of those areas in one product. A data management tool usually covers just one.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > What is a data management platform? > The advertising meaning you may have landed on by mistake
text:
Search this phrase and you'll get a pile of ad-tech results. In marketing, a DMP is a different product. One IT software vendor defines it as software that collects, organizes and deploys data from customers and audiences for use in online campaigns.

If that's what you're after, this guide won't help.

Vendor facts come from each vendor's own pages. We did not run the other tools. We quote no user reviews, and where a vendor shows no price we write "not published."

We left out advertising DMPs, dashboard tools such as Tableau, and tools whose pages we couldn't open. The order inside each group is not a ranking.

Most teams don't need all five jobs on day one. So ask which pain is real, then pick from that lane.

If people can't get to the data, you need a pipeline and a place to store it. If they can reach it but argue about what it means, you need a catalog, rules and a master record.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Start from your problem > Which data management tool fits you?
text:
Question 1 of 5

What is the pain you have today?

The post says to start from the pain, because no single tool does every job.

Tools that move data
Moving data means copying it from apps and databases into that one place.

Tools that move data > 1. Fivetran: for teams that want a vendor to run the pipelines
At a glance: managed service, billed on monthly active rows (MAR), meaning rows that changed in a month.

Fivetran's connector page says 750+ sources, while its pricing page says 700+ fully managed connectors. The two pages disagree, so cite the page you use. Fivetran announced the completion of its merger with dbt Labs in a press release on June 1, 2026 (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Its pricing page lists Free, Standard, Enterprise and Business Critical plans, with a free plan of up to 500,000 MAR a month (checked Oct 2026).
- That page says Standard includes 15-minute syncs, unlimited users, REST API access, SSH tunnels and an integration for dbt Core (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- It says Enterprise adds 1-minute syncs, custom roles, SCIM user provisioning and a Hybrid deployment option (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026). We did not test the sync times, so ask which plan your connector gets.
- Its Managed Data Lake Service docs say Fivetran writes Parquet files to your own cloud storage on Amazon S3, ADLS or GCS and always creates Iceberg metadata for the tables. The limits are below (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Paid per-row rates sit in a separate Service Consumption Table, so your bill depends on your row counts and connections (checked Oct 2026).
- Its destinations docs say your own warehouse provider charges separately for the compute Fivetran uses to load data (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page applies a $5 base charge to standard connections with monthly usage between 1 MAR and 1 million MAR (checked Oct 2026).
- That page says usage counts updates, which it defines as changes to existing rows in your destination, including deletes (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- The Managed Data Lake Service docs say Fivetran does not support position deletes for Iceberg tables. They also say it does not support the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage tiers, because retrieval takes too long (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that move data > 2. Airbyte: for teams that want open-source connectors
text:
At a glance: open source with a self-run Core edition, plus a paid Cloud service billed in credits.

Airbyte's platform docs say it has over 600 pre-built connectors, while its why-open-source page says 700+ (another small mismatch). Its pricing page shows Cloud Standard at $20 a month with 5 credits, then $5 per extra credit (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Its platform docs say it is available as a self-managed, hybrid or fully managed cloud solution.
- They say you can deploy Core locally or in your own infrastructure, and the why-open-source page says to self-host it with `abctl` or Kubernetes (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page shows Plus starting at $189 a month for a 40-credit package, plus a 14-day free trial with 400 credits (checked Oct 2026).
- The Plus card on the pricing page lists enterprise support with a 24-hour response SLA (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Change data capture (CDC) means copying only the rows that changed. Airbyte's CDC docs say syncs are scheduled, and "We do not treat CDC sources as infinite streaming sources." (checked Oct 2026)
- The same CDC docs say CDC incremental is supported only for tables with primary keys for most sources (checked Oct 2026).
- They also say changes made by `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER` do not appear in the logs, so they never reach the destination (CDC docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- A refresh is required after you add a new table or collection to a CDC connection, per the same page (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page's comparison table lists the maximum sync frequency as 1 hour on Standard, 15 minutes on Plus and 5 minutes on Pro and Enterprise Flex. Pro and Enterprise Flex use capacity-based pricing, and the page shows no price for them (checked Oct 2026).
- The why-open-source page lists the connectors and core platform under the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2), which it describes as restricted only for resale as a hosted service (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that move data > 3. OLake Go: for teams that want to copy databases into Iceberg tables they own
text:
At a glance: open-source database replication under Apache 2.0. It copies Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server with a full load and then change capture (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server), and writes Apache Iceberg or Parquet.

OLake Go handles the move step, so pair it with the tools in the later groups for catalog, quality and master data. For support, contact the OLake team.

What's good

- The docs overview lists, per source, full refresh, full refresh plus CDC, CDC only and full refresh plus incremental sync modes, so one tool does the first load and then the change capture.
- Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka also work as sources, without database change capture.
- It writes Iceberg tables to catalogs such as AWS Glue, with eleven catalog types on the catalog compatibility page, or Parquet files on object storage.
- Those catalogs include Snowflake Horizon (OLake Go v0.11.0 and later), BigLake for Google Cloud and Unity Catalog for Databricks.
- Schema discovery runs at the start of every sync, and a new source column is added to the Iceberg schema automatically when Sync new columns automatically is on (schema evolution docs).
- You run it on your own infrastructure with Docker, Helm on Kubernetes or the OLake UI.
- OLake Fusion, a companion product, compacts the Iceberg tables OLake Go writes and shows a health score per table (Fusion docs).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that store and query data
text: A data warehouse is a database built for reports. Lakehouses keep data in cheap file storage but let you query it like a warehouse. All three tools below say they work with the open Apache Iceberg table format: see the Iceberg docs of Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that store and query data > 4. Snowflake: for teams that want a vendor-managed warehouse
text:
At a glance: a managed cloud data platform with a consumption-based price.

Snowflake's pricing page calls its model consumption-based (its own wording: it says it keeps pricing simple), and describes Standard as an entry-level, introductory offering. Its Iceberg docs say Iceberg tables combine Snowflake's query features with external cloud storage that you manage.

What's good

- Snowflake sells four editions: Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical and Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS), which the pricing page says includes all Business Critical features in a completely separate environment (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page says the monthly fee for stored data uses the average amount stored per month, after compression (checked Oct 2026).
- The Iceberg docs say Snowflake supports Iceberg tables that use Parquet files and versions `1`, `2` and `3` of the Iceberg specification, excluding row-level equality deletes (checked Oct 2026).
- They list two catalog options (Iceberg docs): Snowflake as the Iceberg catalog, which gives full platform support with read and write access, or an external catalog such as a remote Iceberg REST catalog, including AWS Glue and Snowflake Open Catalog.
- They also say Snowflake supports externally managed writes for Iceberg tables that use specification version `2` or `3` (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that store and query data > 4. Snowflake: for teams that want a vendor-managed warehouse (part 2)
text:
- The credit consumption table (Table 2(a), effective October 15, 2026) lists $2.00 (Standard), $3.00 (Enterprise) and $4.00 (Business Critical) per credit for AWS, US East (Northern Virginia) (checked Oct 2026). The pricing page has a platform and region picker, so your rate may differ, and a credit rate is not a monthly bill.
- Rates move with region: Table 2(a) of the credit consumption table lists AWS EU Frankfurt at $2.60, $3.90 and $5.20 for the same three editions, and Table 3(a) lists AWS US East storage at $23.00 per terabyte per month on demand (checked Oct 2026).
- Pre-paid capacity is priced as the on-demand rate with a discount set in your order form, and the table does not publish the discount percentages (checked Oct 2026).
- Per the Iceberg docs, an Iceberg table that uses an external catalog gets limited Snowflake platform support. Row-level deletes work only as position deletes on version `2` tables and as deletion vectors on version `3` tables (checked Oct 2026).
- If your Snowflake account and external volume sit in different regions, your external cloud storage account incurs egress costs when you query the table (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that store and query data > 5. Google BigQuery: for teams already on Google Cloud
text:
At a glance: a serverless warehouse. A TiB, the unit it bills queries in by default, is about a trillion bytes.

What's good

- The pricing page says queries are billed per TiB scanned by default and "The first 1 TiB of query data processed per month is free" (checked Oct 2026).
- The first `10 GiB` of storage is also free each month (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Long-term storage covers any table or partition not modified for 90 consecutive days, and its storage price drops automatically by about 50% (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Capacity pricing is available in 3 editions, Standard, Enterprise and Enterprise Plus, and the Standard edition lists slots at $0.04 per hour with no commitment (default view, and the price varies by region and edition) (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Its Iceberg docs say Iceberg managed tables keep data in customer-owned storage buckets and support DML, schema evolution (add, drop and rename columns) and automatic storage optimization.
- They also list an export of an Iceberg `V2` snapshot, refreshed on each table mutation, for engines such as Spark.

Where it falls short

- With on-demand pricing, "you will generally have access to up to 2,000 concurrent slots, shared among all queries in a single project," so busy projects share capacity (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- On-demand charges round up to the nearest MB, with a minimum of `10 MB` per table referenced and per query, and you pay for the data in the columns you select even when you set a `LIMIT` (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- The rendered on-demand rate after the free TiB is $6.25 per TiB, but the table text does not name its region, so check yours (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Per the Iceberg docs, only one mutating DML statement (`UPDATE`, `DELETE` or `MERGE`) runs at a time for each Iceberg managed table, and others queue (checked Oct 2026).
- Iceberg managed tables do not support renaming operations, table copies or table clones (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that store and query data > 6. Databricks: for teams that mix analytics with machine learning
text:
At a glance: a data and AI platform on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, billed pay as you go.

What's good

- The pricing page says "Only pay for the products you use at per second granularity," with no up-front costs (checked Oct 2026).
- It offers committed-use contracts, where larger commitments earn greater discounts, and lists a Free Edition (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Its Iceberg docs say it supports Iceberg tables that use Parquet files and versions `1`, `2` and `3` of the Iceberg specification (the format's own version numbers) (checked Oct 2026).
- They say it supports Iceberg tables managed by Unity Catalog and by foreign catalogs, such as AWS Glue, Hive metastore or Snowflake Horizon Catalog (Iceberg docs).
- Iceberg tables you create in Unity Catalog are managed Iceberg tables (Iceberg docs), and you can create them with Databricks Runtime, Databricks SQL or external engines that support the Iceberg REST Catalog API, such as Apache Spark, Flink, Trino or Kafka.

Where it falls short

- Iceberg tables need Unity Catalog and Databricks Runtime `16.4` LTS (long-term support) or above, and managed tables also need serverless compute (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Foreign Iceberg tables are read-only in Databricks and have limited platform support (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Credential vending is not supported on workspaces that use default storage (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Partition evolution on managed Iceberg tables works through external Iceberg engines using the Iceberg REST Catalog, but not through Databricks SQL (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Serverless compute must have network connectivity to the cloud storage account that backs a managed Iceberg table (Iceberg docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page text we read lists no editions beyond Free Edition and pay as you go (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that catalog and govern data
text:
A data catalog is a searchable inventory of your data, with owners and descriptions. Data governance is the set of rules about who may use data and how. Lineage is a record of where a piece of data came from.

Tools that catalog and govern data > 7. Microsoft Purview: for teams that already run on Microsoft
At a glance: Microsoft's Learn page says Purview helps organizations govern, protect and manage data. It groups security, governance and compliance products, and its governance pieces are Data Map and Unified Catalog.

What's good

- The Learn page says the Purview portal provides access to data governance, data security and data compliance solutions in one place.
- It lists the data security solutions (Learn page) as Data Loss Prevention, Data Security Investigations, Information Barriers, Information Protection and Insider Risk Management.
- The Azure pricing page bills Unified Catalog per governed asset, and the monthly charge for a managed asset is prorated by the days it is governed in the billing cycle (checked Oct 2026).
- Governed assets can be tables, views, AI models and semantic models that are linked to governance concepts (pricing page).
- A Data Map starts at 1 Capacity Unit, which supports up to `25` operations per second and up to `10 GB` of metadata (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Per-unit rates didn't show in the text of the pricing page we fetched. Its own example says 200 governed assets cost $100 for 30 days without discounts (checked Oct 2026).
- Only assets linked to governance concepts count as governed assets, and the Data Map needs an additional Capacity Unit for every `10 GB` of metadata storage (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Governing data in other clouds such as AWS or GCP may incur data transfer and API call charges (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Purview provisions a storage account and an Azure Event Hubs account as managed resources in your subscription, which may carry separate charges that in most cases will not exceed 2% of scanning charges (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Microsoft's Learn page lists Data Security Posture Management as in preview (checked Oct 2026).

Based on the worked example on the Azure Purview pricing page (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that catalog and govern data > 8. Collibra: for large teams with formal governance programs
text:
At a glance: a governance product that, on its product page, says it automates workflows and centralizes policies to create a single source of truth.

What's good

- Its page lists a shared language: a consistent understanding of business terminology, rules and metrics in one location.
- It lists assigning roles and responsibilities to protect data assets from unauthorized access.
- It lists automated compliance checks that flag violations.
- It says AI-driven automation and workflows can speed up curation, classification and governance tasks.
- It says workflows can be embedded into Slack and Microsoft Teams for approvals.
- It says data issues can be submitted, tracked and resolved with automated incident workflows.

Where it falls short

- No price is shown on its product page. The page points to a "Request a demo" button (checked Oct 2026).
- We didn't find the deployment model or a connector count stated on that product page (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that catalog and govern data > 9. OpenMetadata: for teams that want an open-source catalog
text:
At a glance: the OpenMetadata docs home says to document, discover and govern your data assets end to end. Its GitHub page lists the Apache-2.0 licence (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- The docs home lists setup guides for Discovery, Lineage, Observability, Insights, Data Contract and Governance.
- It describes managing data quality checks with version-controlled configurations.
- It lists an upgrade path with compatibility checks and safe rollback options.
- Its Quick Start uses a hosted sandbox or a local Docker setup, so you can try it before you deploy.
- The GitHub page says it comes with 130+ connectors, open metadata standards, semantic search, APIs, SDKs and an MCP server (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- The docs home says to deploy for production using Kubernetes, cloud-managed services or bare metal, so you run and upgrade it yourself unless you buy a managed version (checked Oct 2026).
- We didn't check any managed offering or Iceberg support, so we say nothing about either.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that catalog and govern data > 10. DataHub: for teams that want an open-source catalog with a cloud option
text:
At a glance: the DataHub docs call it a modern data catalog designed to streamline metadata management, data discovery and data governance, and list self-hosting on Kubernetes plus a managed DataHub Cloud. Its GitHub page lists the Apache-2.0 licence (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- The docs say discovery can search dashboards, datasets, ML models and raw files.
- They list governance (define ownership and track PII) and quality and observability (automated anomaly detection, assertions and data contracts).
- They say DataHub supports ingestion by UI and CLI.
- The GitHub page says the self-hosted option has 150+ integrations and column-level lineage.
- DataHub's Google Cloud trial page says a 21-day trial gives you a dedicated Cloud instance managed by the DataHub team, and it lists SLA-backed 99.5% availability for DataHub Cloud (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Self-hosting means running it yourself: the docs say to start with a CLI command or deploy to production with Docker or Helm charts, and the GitHub page calls self-hosting best for teams comfortable running their own stack.
- The trial page lists enterprise lineage views, governance workflows and AI capabilities as not available in open source (checked Oct 2026).
- DataHub publishes no DataHub Cloud price that we could find on its site or the trial page (checked Oct 2026), so we state none.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that catalog and govern data > 11. Great Expectations: for teams that write Python
text:
At a glance: the Great Expectations docs say its Core library is a Python library for building and running data validation workflows, built around rules called expectations. The repository licence is Apache 2.0 (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- The docs define an Expectation as a verifiable assertion about data.
- Every workflow follows the same four steps: set up an environment, connect to data, define Expectations and run Validations.
- Actions can send validation results as email, Slack or Microsoft Teams alerts.
- Data Docs are human-readable pages that hold your Expectation Suite definitions and Validation Results.
- You can apply the same Expectation Suite to different Batches of data.

Where it falls short

- It validates data, so you write the rules yourself and run them in code.
- The docs' scheduled-testing example needs an orchestrator to trigger the workflow.
- Its blog post of May 2026 announced that GX Cloud would no longer be publicly available beginning June 1.
- The same post says Fivetran will become the steward of the open-source community and GX Core, which it says will continue as an open-source, community-driven project.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > Tools that manage master data
text:
Sales has one customer list and finance has another. Master data is the core list of things your business cares about, such as customers and products, and master data management (MDM) keeps one trusted record of each so nobody holds two versions.

Tools that manage master data > 12. Informatica: for large companies that want many data jobs from one vendor
At a glance: Informatica's MDM page describes MDM as the process of creating and maintaining a single, trusted record for customers, products and more. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Informatica on November 18, 2025, per Salesforce's press release.

What's good

- Its site lists catalog, integration, quality, MDM and governance products, so it spans several of the five jobs.
- Its pricing page says Informatica Processing Units (IPUs) give access to all eligible cloud services listed in its Cloud and Product Description Schedule (checked Oct 2026).
- The page's menu lists Free Cloud Data Integration (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- The Cloud and Product Description Schedule (version `39.2.1`, effective October 21, 2026) shows Database Ingestion and Replication CDC falling from 6.5 IPU per million rows for the first 15 million to 0.55 up to 750 million and 0.05 above that (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- The pricing page explains IPUs, a usage meter, and ends with a "Get Quote" button. No dollar price per unit appears, and the rates by service live in the separate schedule, so get a quote before you budget (checked Oct 2026).
- Under the IPU model, unused IPUs do not carry over to the next month, and under the Flex IPU model they are consumed over an annual period instead (schedule) (checked Oct 2026).

- IPU and Flex IPU must be provisioned separately and may not be deployed in the same Org (schedule) (checked Oct 2026).
- The schedule does not say whether a volume tier applies to your whole quantity or only to the units inside each band (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > How to choose a data management platform
text:
- Name the pain. Data people can't reach needs a pipeline and a store. Data they don't trust needs a catalog, quality checks or master data.
- Check the meter. Rows, credits, scanned bytes, governed assets and processing units all grow differently, and that's where bills surprise people.
- Count who will run it. Open-source tools are free to license, but they still need servers and people.
- Ask for the missing price in writing. Collibra, Semarchy and Informatica each want you to ask for a quote.
- Test one tool before adding a second. Add jobs once the first one works.

Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks all document support for Apache Iceberg, an open table format for data kept in your own storage (see the Iceberg docs of Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks). If you keep data there, the copy step matters a lot. OLake Go, covered in the first group above, writes Iceberg tables through catalogs those platforms use: Snowflake Horizon, BigLake and Unity Catalog.

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > The short version, again
text:
A data management platform is a set of jobs: move the data, store it, find it, check it and agree on one master record. Match each job to a tool, and add them in the order your problems show up.

The cheapest way to start is usually a free tier or an open-source tool for the first job. If a vendor doesn't publish a price, ask for a written quote before you commit.

Q1. What is a data management platform?

It's software that covers several parts of managing a company's data, such as moving, storing, cataloging and checking it. The DMBOK framework lists 11 areas of data management, and no vendor page we checked claims all 11. In advertising the same words mean a different product, one that builds audience groups for ad targeting.

Q2. Is a data management platform the same as a customer data platform?

Not in the advertising sense. One IT vendor's guide says an advertising DMP works with anonymous audience data for shorter campaigns, while a customer data platform keeps named individual profiles. An enterprise data management platform is a third thing again, aimed at your company's own operational and analytical data.

Q3. Do I need one platform or several tools?

It depends on your team. One suite means one contract and fewer connections to build. Several tools mean more choice and often a lower starting cost, and you can see the split in this list: Informatica and Microsoft Purview bundle several products, while Fivetran and Great Expectations each do one job.

Q4. What is the difference between data management and data governance?

Governance is one of the 11 areas in the DMBOK framework. It sets the rules about who may use data and how, while data management is the bigger umbrella that also includes storage, integration, quality and more.

Q5. Which data management tools are free?

OpenMetadata, DataHub and Great Expectations are open source under the Apache-2.0 licence, Airbyte Core is free to self-host under the Elastic License 2.0, and OLake Go is open source under Apache 2.0. Fivetran has a free plan of up to 500,000 rows a month, and BigQuery gives you the first 1 TiB of queries each month free (checked Oct 2026). Free software still needs servers and people to run it.

Q6. What is master data management?

title: Compare: Best Data Management Platforms and Tools (2026) | OLake > The short version, again (part 2)
text:
It's the practice of keeping one trusted record for each customer, product or supplier. Informatica describes it as creating and maintaining a single, trusted record across your business. Semarchy and Informatica both sell MDM tools, and neither publishes a full price.

Q7. How much do data management tools cost?

Anywhere from free open source to quote-only contracts. Airbyte Cloud Standard starts at $20 a month with 5 credits, per its pricing page (checked Oct 2026), and Purview's own example is $100 for 200 governed assets over 30 days (checked Oct 2026). Collibra, Semarchy and Informatica's per-unit rate aren't published, so you'll need a quote.

Q8. Which data management tool should I buy first?

Buy for the pain you have today. If people can't reach data, start with a pipeline such as Fivetran, Airbyte or OLake Go. If they can reach it but don't trust it, start with a catalog or quality checks such as OpenMetadata or Great Expectations, and add master data later.

Q9. Why do data management tools bill in so many different units?

Fivetran counts monthly active rows, Airbyte Cloud counts credits, BigQuery counts TiB scanned, Purview counts governed assets, and Informatica counts processing units. Before you compare prices, ask which unit will grow fastest for you.

title: Compare: Best Data Pipeline Tools in 2026, by Job | OLake
text:
Key takeaways

Short version: there's no single best data pipeline tool, because a pipeline has four jobs and most tools only do one. Fivetran, Airbyte, Hevo, OLake Go and Debezium load your data. Kafka and Flink handle streams, dbt reshapes data once it has landed, and Airflow, Dagster and Prefect run the steps in order.

Matillion, AWS Glue and Azure Data Factory bundle several jobs inside one vendor's cloud, so pick one tool per job (or one bundle) and check how each one bills.

- Don't compare unlike tools. Airflow won't copy your database, dbt doesn't load anything, and Kafka itself doesn't reshape warehouse tables. They sit side by side in a stack.
- Billing meters differ a lot. Fivetran counts changed rows, Hevo counts events, Airbyte and Dagster count credits, dbt counts models built, and AWS Glue counts compute time.
- Free isn't zero. Most of the 14 tools have free software or a free plan, each with a ceiling, and open-source tools still cost servers and people.

We checked prices against each vendor's own pages in October 2026.

title: Compare: Best Data Pipeline Tools in 2026, by Job | OLake > So what is a "data pipeline tool", anyway?
text:
A data pipeline is a series of processing steps that prepare enterprise data for analysis, which is broad enough to cover almost anything. A pipeline has four jobs, and a tool built for one usually isn't built for the others.

- Ingest: copy data from where it lives, such as a database or an app, to a new place.
- Store: keep it in a warehouse (a database built for reports) or a data lake (cheap file storage many tools can read).
- Transform: clean, join and reshape the data so people can use it.
- Orchestrate: run the other steps on a schedule, in the right order, and retry or alert when one fails.

Reshape data before it lands and that's called extract, transform, load (ETL). Reshape it after and it's extract, load, transform (ELT). Streaming is a way of doing the first and third jobs: instead of moving data in batches every hour, a streaming tool handles each change as it happens.

A scheduler doesn't move or reshape a single row. It starts the other tools in the right order and alerts you when one fails.
