title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The two bills (and why they matter)
text:
Snowflake sells compute as credits.

In Snowflake's Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026), an `X-Small` warehouse uses 1 credit per hour. One credit costs $2.00 on the Standard edition in AWS US East (Northern Virginia). Other editions and regions cost more. Enterprise is $3.00 in the same region, and AWS EU Frankfurt is $2.60 on Standard.

A loader that runs often keeps a warehouse awake, and Snowflake bills you for that time, not the tool. So a tool with a cheap sticker price can still add up to a big Snowflake bill.

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > Worked example: what a faster sync does to your Snowflake bill
text:
This example uses only the documented rates above, plus one assumption of ours: each sync keeps an `X-Small` warehouse awake for 3 minutes, including the minute before it suspends.

Fivetran's Snowflake documentation says Snowflake bills compute per second, and recommends an `X-Small` warehouse with one-minute auto-suspend. Our 3-minute figure is an assumption for illustration.

| Sync every | Syncs a day | Warehouse minutes a day | Credits a day | Cost a day at $2.00 | Cost over 30 days |
| 60 minutes | 24 | 72 | 1.2 | $2.40 | $72 |
| 15 minutes | 96 | 288 | 4.8 | $9.60 | $288 |
| 5 minutes | 288 | 864 | 14.4 | $28.80 | $864 |

Sources: the $2.00 and $3.00 credit prices are from the Snowflake Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026). The sync counts and minutes are our own assumptions.

The tool fee stayed put, and only the Snowflake side changed, by a factor of 12 between hourly and every 5 minutes. On Enterprise at $3.00 a credit, multiply every cost by 1.5.

Ask how fresh your data needs to be. A dashboard that someone reads once a morning doesn't need a 5-minute sync.

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Built into Snowflake
text:
**1. Snowflake loading ( COPY INTO , Snowpipe, Snowpipe Streaming): for data that already lands as files or rows**

At a glance

- Billed by: Snowflake credits. Snowpipe is 0.0037 credits per GB, with text files such as CSV and JSON counted at uncompressed size, per the Snowflake Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026)
- Price: Snowpipe Streaming (high-performance architecture) is also 0.0037 credits per uncompressed GB, so about $0.0074 per GB at $2.00 a credit, per the same table (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active, part of Snowflake

Snowflake's data loading overview lists four ways in. `COPY INTO` (a command that loads files already in cloud storage) handles batches. Snowpipe loads small batches and makes them available within minutes after files reach a stage.

Snowpipe Streaming writes rows straight to tables without staged files. A Kafka connector reads topics from an Apache Kafka server.

What's good

- Snowflake says Snowpipe Streaming is designed for ingest speeds of up to 20 GB/s per table, with ingest-to-queryable latency as low as 5 seconds. It adds that results depend on workload shape and configuration (Snowpipe Streaming overview).
- The same page gives a plain rule for picking a path. Use Snowpipe Streaming when data arrives as rows from applications, devices or services and you need low latency. Use Snowpipe when your pipeline already produces files in cloud storage and batch-style loading is fine.
- Snowflake's docs say Snowpipe Streaming can stream rows into Snowflake tables or into Snowflake-managed Apache Iceberg tables (checked Oct 2026), so the Iceberg column in the table above needs no second vendor here.
- Snowflake's Service Consumption Table says binary files such as Parquet, Avro and ORC are charged for their observed size whatever the compression. Classic Snowpipe Streaming is 0.01 credits per client instance per hour (checked Oct 2026).
- Warehouse time is billed per second after a 60-second minimum, and a suspended warehouse does not use any credits per the Snowflake compute cost docs (checked Oct 2026). That is the rule behind the worked example above.

Choose it if your applications or an upstream tool already produce files in cloud storage or rows in a stream, and you'd rather not add another vendor.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Built into Snowflake (part 2)
text:
- These are loading features, not source connectors. Something else has to read your database or SaaS app and produce the files or rows.
- `COPY INTO` plus your own scripts means you write and run the scheduling, retries and schema handling yourself.
- Snowflake's Snowpipe docs (checked Oct 2026) say it is very difficult for Snowflake to estimate Snowpipe latency. They also say that while Snowpipe generally loads older files first, there is no guarantee files load in the order they were staged.
- Snowpipe keeps each loaded file's path and name and will not load a file with the same name again, even if the file was changed afterwards (Snowpipe docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Snowflake recommends data files of roughly `100` to `250 MB` compressed, or larger. Snowpipe's cost includes an overhead for managing queued files that grows with the number of files waiting, so many small files raise the cost (file preparation guide) (checked Oct 2026).

**2. Snowflake Openflow: for teams who want Snowflake to run the connector**

At a glance

- Billed by: vCPUs used by connector runtimes, per second with a 60-second minimum, for active runtimes only, per Snowflake's Openflow cost page (checked Oct 2026)
- Price: 0.0225 credits per vCPU-hour on BYOC (bring your own cloud), plus your cloud provider bill and Snowpipe charges for the data (Openflow cost page) (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: generally available. Snowflake's Openflow overview (checked Oct 2026) says Snowflake-run deployments are open to all accounts in AWS, Azure and Google Cloud Commercial regions, and BYOC deployments to AWS Commercial regions only. Its connectors page lists AWS Commercial regions only.

Openflow is "built on Apache NiFi", an open-source dataflow tool, and its connectors are curated NiFi flow definitions. Snowflake's Openflow cost page (checked Oct 2026) says database change data capture (CDC, reading a database's change log) connectors need a Snowflake warehouse. That covers both the first copy and the ongoing changes.

Connector families include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server and MongoDB, plus SaaS apps and Kafka (connectors page).

Snowflake's own cost example adds up 84 vCPU-hours. That is 84 × 0.0225 = 1.89 credits, or about $3.78 at $2.00 a credit (checked Oct 2026). That is before the cloud bill for the servers.

What's good

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Built into Snowflake (part 3)
text:
- Two deployment types. In BYOC the data plane runs in your own cloud while Snowflake manages the service and control plane. The Snowflake deployment uses Snowpark Container Services (Openflow overview).
- The connectors page lists SQL Server twice: a change tracking (CT) connector and a CDC connector that captures every row-level change. It also lists BigQuery with incremental change capture, Kafka and Kinesis Data Streams, and Salesforce Bulk API with incremental change detection.
- Snowflake's cost page says database CDC connectors need a warehouse for both the first snapshot and ongoing changes, and that you can schedule `MERGE` operations to manage that compute cost.
- Snowflake's docs say the PostgreSQL connector can write Snowflake-managed Apache Iceberg tables as an opt-in format. Iceberg `v2` and `v3` are both supported, and storage can be Snowflake storage or an external volume in your own cloud storage (PostgreSQL Iceberg page, a Preview feature).
- The MongoDB connector copies each selected collection in full once, then follows MongoDB change streams on a schedule (MongoDB connector page).

Choose it if you already pay Snowflake, run on AWS (or use a Snowflake-run deployment elsewhere), and like the idea of database CDC with one vendor and one contract.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Built into Snowflake (part 4)
text:
- Most connectors on the connectors page (checked Oct 2026) bring data into Snowflake, which is our reading of the list, so Openflow fits best when Snowflake is where your data ends up.
- The Oracle connector has its own licence in the credit table: $70 per licensed core per month on a 36-month commitment, plus support (checked Oct 2026).
- The overview page (checked Oct 2026) says any new deployment is gen 2, and that gen 2 connector configuration remains in Public Preview.
- Openflow is not automatically available in trial accounts. The overview page (checked Oct 2026) says to contact your Snowflake account team to enable it.
- The PostgreSQL Iceberg page (checked Oct 2026) carries a Preview Feature banner. Snowflake says not to change the `Table Storage Format` or the `Iceberg Version` after the connector starts.
- The MongoDB connector page (checked Oct 2026) carries a Preview label. It does not support standalone MongoDB instances and relies on the `oplog`. It needs MongoDB `4.4` or later and supports username and password authentication only. Each document's whole payload lands in one `data` column next to its `id`.

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Managed ELT services you pay a vendor to run
text:
**3. Fivetran: for vendor-run connectors**

At a glance

- Billed by: monthly active rows (MAR), meaning rows that changed in a month, counted per connection
- Price: Free up to 500,000 MAR; $5 base charge for 1 to 1M MAR; Standard from $495 per million MAR, Enterprise $661.67, Business Critical $1,061.67 (per connection, list price, from its Service Consumption Table) (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active; merged with dbt Labs on June 1, 2026

Fivetran counts rows that changed, and it counts them per connection. Fivetran's pricing page lists Free, Standard, Enterprise and Business Critical plans (checked Oct 2026).

Its Snowflake destination docs cover native tables, or Lakehouse tables (Beta), which are Iceberg tables that Fivetran manages in its own data lake service and Snowflake reads. The merger with dbt Labs is in Fivetran's press release.

What's good

- Its sync overview lists sync frequencies from 1 minute to 24 hours. The default is every 6 hours in fixed interval mode, and cron schedules are also offered.
- Its database connectors docs say incremental changes come from the source's own change mechanism where one exists (MySQL and MariaDB binary log, PostgreSQL logical replication, MongoDB change streams, SQL Server CDC or change tracking), or from a Fivetran method such as Teleport Sync.
- The same database connectors page says database connectors sync new and modified data every 15 minutes by default, update the destination in batches with a merge operation, and that most initial syncs finish within a day.
- Fivetran's pricing page lists unlimited users, 700+ fully managed connectors and an Integration for dbt Core on Standard (checked Oct 2026).
- The same pricing page lists 1-minute syncs, custom roles, SCIM and a Hybrid deployment option on Enterprise. Business Critical adds customer-managed keys, PCI DSS Level 1 certification and private networking options (checked Oct 2026).

Choose it if you want a vendor to own connector upkeep (Fivetran's pitch, not tested by us) for many SaaS apps and databases, and you'd rather pay a meter than hire an engineer.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Managed ELT services you pay a vendor to run (part 2)
text:
- The meter counts changed rows. Our read: a busy table nobody looks at can cost more than the summary table your dashboards actually use.
- Lakehouse tables are Beta, per Fivetran's Snowflake destination docs (checked Oct 2026).
- The same docs (checked Oct 2026) say the maximum length for `VARIANT` and `VARCHAR` columns is `128 MB`, and Fivetran truncates values that exceed it.
- The pricing page lists 15-minute syncs for Standard. The sync overview says 1-minute syncs need an Enterprise or Business Critical plan and are not supported for any Lite connector (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing page FAQ counts Oracle and High-Volume Agent connectors as enterprise database connectors. The Enterprise plan lists that group, and Standard lists plain database connectors (checked Oct 2026).
- The database connectors page (checked Oct 2026) says schema changes in the source are the most common trigger for a full table re-sync. It also says expired change logs require a full source re-sync, and that Teleport Sync may re-sync a whole table if you update large portions of it between syncs.

**4. Hevo: for small teams that want a free plan**

At a glance

- Billed by: events, which count records inserted, updated or deleted at the source
- Price: Free is $0 for 1M events a month; Starter is $299 monthly or $265 billed yearly from 5M events, per Hevo's pricing page (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active

Hevo's pricing page shows a free plan, a 14-day trial with no card, and Starter and Professional tiers (checked Oct 2026).

Hevo's docs list Snowflake as a standard destination. A separate Snowflake Iceberg destination (checked Oct 2026) is described as loading into Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables with files in your S3 bucket, and it's in Early Access.

The same page warns that Snowflake is deprecating password sign-in and enforcing multi-factor authentication, so Hevo recommends key pair authentication. Plan for it with any loader.

What's good

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Managed ELT services you pay a vendor to run (part 3)
text:
- Hevo's log-based pipelines page lists the change source for each database: BinLog for MySQL, logical replication for PostgreSQL, Change Streams or OpLog for MongoDB, Change Tracking for SQL Server and redo logs for Oracle.
- Per Hevo's pricing page (checked Oct 2026), Free covers limited connectors, up to 5 users and 1-hour scheduling. Starter, Professional and Business Critical list all available connectors.
- Hevo's events usage docs say that on plans from Release `1.48` onwards, going over the events quota starts a grace period to buy more events while pipelines keep running.
- Its Snowflake Iceberg (Edge) docs say the table data and metadata files sit in your own S3 bucket. They also say external engines such as Apache Spark and Trino can read the tables through the Horizon Iceberg REST Catalog API.

Choose it if you're a small team with common sources and want a free start.

Where it falls short

- Hevo's events usage docs (checked Oct 2026) say inserted and updated events at the source are billable, so a busy table costs more (a row changed five times is five events, our reading). They add that events deleted at the source are billable as updates.
- The same docs (checked Oct 2026) say Hevo charges the selected plan price whether or not you use the full capacity of the plan.
- The log-based pipelines page (checked Oct 2026) says streaming pipelines, available from Release `2.21`, cover those source types except SQL Server and DynamoDB, and that you must contact Hevo Sales to enable streaming.
- The Iceberg docs (checked Oct 2026) say the destination is currently available for Early Access and is enabled through a Hevo account executive or Support.
- The Iceberg docs (checked Oct 2026) list prerequisites of a Snowflake account on AWS, an S3 bucket with an IAM policy for Snowflake, and an external volume in Snowflake.

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Open source, source-available and streaming
text:
**5. Airbyte: for a large connector catalog you can self-host**

At a glance

- Billed by: credits on Cloud; nothing for Core, which you run yourself
- Price: Cloud Standard is $20 a month with 5 credits, then $5 per extra credit, per Airbyte's Cloud release notes (the September 23, 2026 entry) (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active

Airbyte Core is free to run yourself under the Elastic License 2.0 (per Airbyte's licence FAQ). That licence does not allow offering the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service. Its Snowflake destination loads through a Snowflake stage. Airbyte's docs give the same advice as Fivetran's: a small, dedicated warehouse with a one-minute auto-suspend.

What's good

- Airbyte's CDC docs list current support for Postgres, MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, MongoDB, Oracle DB, SAP HANA and IBM Db2. The page does not say which plan or connector support level covers Oracle, SAP HANA and Db2.
- The same docs say the first CDC sync takes a snapshot of the current data with a `SELECT`, and later syncs read the logs from the previously synced position.
- Cloud usage is metered in credits. Per Airbyte's credits docs (checked Oct 2026), databases and files use 4 credits per GB, and APIs and custom sources use 6 credits per million rows.
- The credits docs also say that if you run out of credits, Cloud keeps your syncs running and bills you in arrears. It does not stop in-progress syncs or pause scheduled ones. Trials last 14 days or 400 credits, whichever comes first (checked Oct 2026).
- Its Snowflake destination docs say Airbyte loads through Snowflake's internal stage and supports Full Refresh Overwrite, Overwrite + Deduped and Append, plus Incremental Append and Append + Deduped.
- The Cloud release notes list a Plus tier that starts at a 40-credit package, with a 15-minute sync frequency, two workspaces, single sign-on and premium support. They also say unused Cloud credits now roll over for 3 months (checked Oct 2026).

Choose it if you've got engineers and want a large connector catalog, with a cloud option later. Airbyte's home page says 700+ connectors and its GitHub page says 600+; we did not count.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Open source, source-available and streaming (part 2)
text:
- Airbyte's CDC docs (checked Oct 2026) say CDC runs as scheduled syncs, not as a continuous stream.
- Self-hosting moves the bill to servers and staff, and Airbyte's pricing page does not publish prices for Pro and Enterprise Flex (checked Oct 2026).
- The CDC docs (checked Oct 2026) say CDC incremental sync works only for tables with primary keys for most sources. Changes made by `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER` do not appear in the logs, so they do not reach the destination, and a refresh is required after you add a new table to a CDC connection.
- Airbyte's connector support levels page (checked Oct 2026) says Marketplace connectors are maintained by community members, are not covered by Airbyte support SLAs, and may see breaking changes with no notice. Enterprise connectors are not available to Open Source or standard Cloud customers.
- Airbyte's credits docs (checked Oct 2026) say that for Full Refresh syncs of APIs and custom sources, every row synced is charged.
- The Snowflake destination docs (checked Oct 2026) say Snowflake is enforcing strong authentication on a rolling per-account basis between August and October 2026. Once it is enforced, password-only logins from Airbyte fail, and key pair authentication is the only recommended method since version `5.0.0`.

**6. Estuary: for real-time capture with a free tier**

At a glance

- Billed by: gigabytes moved plus connector instances
- Price: $0.50 per GB; the first 6 instances are $100 a month each, then $50 each; Free is 10 GB and 2 instances, per Estuary's pricing page (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active

Estuary's pricing page (checked Oct 2026) counts each source and each destination as one instance, so one source feeding Snowflake is two. Its Snowflake connector uploads changes to a Snowflake stage and applies them in transactions, and an option called `delta updates` can use Snowpipe Streaming (it's off by default).

What's good

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Open source, source-available and streaming (part 3)
text:
- Update mode is set per binding on the Snowflake connector. Standard (merge) updates are the default, and `delta updates` can be switched on for a binding. Delta bindings use Snowpipe Streaming by default and need key pair authentication to do so (Estuary's Snowflake docs).
- Estuary's sync schedule docs say warehouse connectors such as Snowflake support a sync schedule, and that the `Sync Frequency` setting defaults to `30 minutes` if unset. Syncing less often does not change what the connector costs inside Estuary but can reduce the costs in the destination.
- Per Estuary's pricing page (checked Oct 2026), a new pipeline runs a historical backfill and then switches to real-time CDC, and the backfill can be disabled or scoped. Adding a new target means paying only for the added target and the data sent to it, with no re-extract from each source.
- The pricing FAQ says the 30-day free trial starts automatically once you pass the free tier limits, gives access to all Cloud plan features, and needs no credit card (checked Oct 2026).
- The Enterprise column lists SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance reports, single sign-on, custom SLA terms, and private and BYOC deployments (annual contract only) (checked Oct 2026).

Choose it if you want to test low-latency change capture into Snowflake (Estuary's claim, which we did not test) without handing over a card.

Where it falls short

- Each extra destination adds $50 to $100 a month, so count your instances before you commit (pricing page) (checked Oct 2026).
- Its licence is the Business Source License 1.1, which Estuary's repository (checked Oct 2026) says is not an open-source licence.
- Estuary's pricing docs say data movement into and out of Estuary is priced at $0.50 per GB (checked Oct 2026). The pricing page's own calculator example (800 GB, 2 connector instances) shows a higher monthly total than 800 GB at $0.50 per GB plus the two instance fees would give. Our arithmetic is that the gap matches 800 GB counted both in and out.
- The Cloud plan lists standard support via community Slack and email. The Enterprise column is where custom SLA terms are listed (checked Oct 2026).
- The pricing docs say Private and BYOC deployments need an annual plan and add fees based on the cloud infrastructure required. No figure is published (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Open source, source-available and streaming (part 4)
text:
**7. OLake Go: for database sources into Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database**

At a glance

- Billed by: nothing; you run it on your own servers
- Price: free, open source under Apache 2.0
- Status: active; Snowflake Horizon Catalog support starts in OLake Go v0.11.0 (release notes)

OLake Go is not a `COPY INTO` style loader. It creates Apache Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database through the Snowflake Horizon Catalog, used as an Iceberg REST (web API) catalog (our Horizon docs). Change capture covers Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server), and our docs also list Kafka and S3 as sources.

What's good

- Authentication by programmatic access token (PAT), key pair or External OAuth.
- Our docs ask for a Snowflake database with catalog `SNOWFLAKE` and external volume `SNOWFLAKE_MANAGED`, or your own external volume for AWS, GCP or Azure storage.
- Our compatibility page ticks positional deletes and deletion vectors for Snowflake. The Target Query Engine setting shows only the upsert types your engine reads.

Choose it if your sources are databases, Kafka topics or S3 files and you want open-source software that lands them as Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database.

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Transformation and enterprise suites
text:
**8. Matillion: for visual pipelines that run inside Snowflake**

At a glance

- Billed by: credits for run time, at 1 credit per task hour for orchestration and 3 for transformation, plus developer users, per Matillion's credit terms (checked Oct 2026)
- Price: not published; the pricing page shows credits and no price per credit (checked Oct 2026)
- Status: active; renamed from Data Productivity Cloud to Maia in early 2026, per its terminology changes page (checked Oct 2026)

Matillion's pricing page (checked Oct 2026) lists editions without a dollar price.

Matillion's own comparison page says transformations run as SQL pushed down into Snowflake. The work uses your Snowflake warehouse and you pay Snowflake for it.

Matillion's streaming docs say change capture is limited to specific plans and to relational sources: Db2 for i, SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL.

What's good

- Per Matillion's pricing page (checked Oct 2026), the Developer card lists 1 developer user, unlimited projects, pre-built connectors, a low-code canvas with SQL and Python, and a built-in Git repository. Maia is available to trial for free on a time-bound, fair-use basis.
- The Teams card adds 5 developer users, an audit log, standard customer support and a service level agreement. The Scale card lists custom SSO, hybrid cloud deployment, data lineage tracking, streaming change data capture, log retention of 180+ days and bring-your-own Git.
- The pricing FAQ says you can contract directly with Matillion or pay through your AWS, Azure or Snowflake account.
- Matillion's streaming pipelines docs list Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage and Snowflake as destinations, and describe "near-real-time data ingestion". The streaming runner is a service you deploy in your own cloud infrastructure.
- Its credit terms put streaming pipelines at 1 credit per task hour for an essential CDC pipeline and 2 for a premium one. Task use is measured in 2-second increments (checked Oct 2026).

Choose it if your team likes a visual designer and most of the work is transformation inside Snowflake.

Where it falls short

text:
- The price is not published on the pricing page (checked Oct 2026), so you'll need a quote before you can plan anything.

**9. Informatica: for large companies with older sources**

At a glance

- Billed by: Informatica Processing Units (IPU), which each service uses up every month
- Price: AWS Marketplace lists a bundle of 120 IPUs a month at $131,760 for 12 months, per the listing (checked Oct 2026); the Informatica pages we read show no price per IPU
- Status: active; the product schedule carries a Salesforce, Inc. copyright notice (checked Oct 2026)

Informatica's database replication docs list sources such as Db2, Oracle, SQL Server, SAP (a business software maker), Teradata, MySQL and PostgreSQL. They also list Snowflake as a target, including Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables. Treat a marketplace price as a list price, not a quote.

What's good

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Transformation and enterprise suites (part 3)
text:
- In Informatica's database ingestion and replication docs, Db2 (for i, LUW and z/OS), SQL Server, MongoDB, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL and SAP HANA are each marked supported for initial, incremental and combined loads.

Database Ingestion and Replication is 0.1 IPU per GB for the first 2 TB and steps down through four tiers to 0.018 above 25 TB. Its CDC rate is 6.5 IPU per million rows for the first 15M rows, 0.55 up to 750M and 0.05 above (checked Oct 2026).

**10. dbt and dynamic tables: for SQL transforms after the load**

At a glance

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > The 10 best ETL tools for Snowflake > Transformation and enterprise suites (part 4)
text:
- Billed by: dbt charges developer seats and successful models built; dynamic tables use Snowflake credits
- Price: dbt Developer is free for 1 seat and `3,000` models a month; Starter is $100 per user per month, per dbt's pricing page (checked Oct 2026)

dbt turns SQL select statements into tested tables, and it needs a loader to run first. Snowflake's own answer is dynamic tables, which keep the result of a query up to date with a minimum `target lag` of `60 seconds`. They cost warehouse compute, cloud services and storage, so the more often they refresh, the more you pay.

What's good

- dbt's data tests docs list four built-in generic tests: `unique`, `not_null`, `accepted_values` and `relationships`. Singular tests are plain SQL that returns the failing rows, and open-source packages such as `dbt-utils` and `dbt-expectations` add more generic tests.
- Per dbt's pricing page (checked Oct 2026), Starter includes five developer seats, `15,000` successful models built a month and `5,000` queried metrics.
- dbt's billing docs say only models that build successfully are counted. If a job of 100 models fails after 51 are built, 51 count.
- Snowflake runs managed dbt Core and dbt Fusion runtimes for dbt Projects on Snowflake. Executions use a virtual warehouse and standard compute costs, with no additional Snowflake licensing or per-user fees (Snowflake's dbt Projects docs).
- Snowflake's dynamic tables docs say they suit workloads that want results to stay up to date without custom orchestration code, and multi-step pipelines with joins, aggregations or window functions. It also says you can move from batch to near-real-time freshness by changing a single parameter, the `target lag`.

Choose it if your raw data is already in Snowflake and your team writes SQL. dbt suits tested, version-controlled projects, while dynamic tables suit teams that want no extra tool.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > FAQs
text:
Q1. What is the best ETL tool for Snowflake?

It depends on your source. Snowflake's own Snowpipe adds no second vendor fee if files already exist, so price it first. Fivetran, Hevo and Airbyte fit many SaaS sources, Estuary or Openflow fit live database changes, and OLake Go fits open-source database replication into Iceberg in Snowflake. Pick by source type, freshness, and the total of the tool fee plus Snowflake credits.

Q2. Is Snowflake used for ETL or ELT?

Often ELT. Tools load the raw data first, then the reshaping runs inside Snowflake with SQL, using dbt, Matillion or dynamic tables. Snowflake's compute does that transform work, so it shows up on your Snowflake bill.

Q3. Does Snowflake have built-in ETL tools?

Yes, for loading. You get `COPY INTO`, Snowpipe, Snowpipe Streaming, a Kafka connector and Openflow connectors, plus dynamic tables for transforms. What it doesn't ship is a connector for every source, so you may add Fivetran, Airbyte or Hevo for the rest.

Q4. How much does it cost to load data into Snowflake?

Two costs add up: the tool vendor's fee and Snowflake credits. In Snowflake's Service Consumption Table (checked Oct 2026), an `X-Small` warehouse uses 1 credit per hour, and a credit is $2.00 on Standard in AWS US East. Snowpipe is 0.0037 credits per GB on top of that rate.

Q5. Do I need dbt if I use Fivetran or Airbyte?

They load data, and the transform layer is a separate choice. Fivetran's pricing page lists an Integration for dbt Core (checked Oct 2026), and Fivetran merged with dbt Labs on June 1, 2026. You can also use dbt or Snowflake dynamic tables. Our read: choose the one your SQL team will actually maintain.

Q6. Can these tools write Iceberg tables that Snowflake reads?

Several can. Fivetran's Lakehouse tables are Beta, and Hevo's Snowflake Iceberg destination is Early Access and uses an Amazon S3 bucket. Snowpipe Streaming can also write Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables, and OLake Go (v0.11.0 and later) creates Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database through the Horizon Catalog. Check the catalog and storage you need before you commit.

Q7. How fresh can data in Snowflake be?

title: Compare: Best ETL Tools for Snowflake: 10 Options, Real Costs | OLake > FAQs (part 2)
text:
Snowpipe loads within minutes after files reach a stage, and dynamic tables have a minimum `target lag` of `60 seconds`. Hevo's Free plan uses 1-hour scheduling (checked Oct 2026). Faster refresh uses more warehouse time, so set it to what your readers actually need.

Q8. Should I skip a third-party tool and use only Snowpipe?

Yes, if your data already lands as files in cloud storage or as rows from your own app. Snowpipe and Snowpipe Streaming load those without another vendor. The catch is that you still need something to read databases or SaaS apps and produce the files or rows.

Q9. How does OLake Go work with Snowflake?

Two ways. From v0.11.0, OLake Go creates Iceberg tables in a Snowflake database through the Horizon Catalog (our docs). Snowflake also queries OLake Go's Iceberg tables as one of the engines on our compatibility page, and tables from external catalogs are read-only in Snowflake.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake
text:
Key takeaways

SQL Server already has change data capture (CDC) built in, and most tools below simply read from it. Microsoft's docs say native CDC needs SQL Server Agent running and keeps changes for three days by default (checked Oct 2026).

Pick by where the data has to land and who will run the pipeline. Debezium suits Kafka teams, Fivetran suits vendor-run loads, and Airbyte suits scheduled loads you run yourself. Qlik Replicate and Striim suit large estates, AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) suits AWS teams, Datastream suits Google Cloud, and Fabric mirroring suits Microsoft Fabric.

- Native SQL Server CDC is a feature of the database, not a tool. SQL Server Agent jobs copy changes from the transaction log into change tables.
- Retention is the clock that breaks pipelines. Miss the three-day default window and you're starting over.
- Schema changes are the second trap. A new column isn't captured until you add a second capture instance (Microsoft).

We read each vendor's own documentation on 8 October 2026. We quote no list prices here.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > How SQL Server CDC works, in plain terms
text:
Change data capture means spotting the inserts, updates and deletes in a database and sending only those on. In SQL Server, Microsoft's CDC docs say the source of change data is the transaction log, the file where the database records every change in order.

A job called the capture job reads that log and writes the changes into change tables. Each tracked table gets a capture instance, which is one change table plus up to two query functions. By default the instance is named `schema_table`, and its change table gets `_CT` added, per Microsoft.

Every change row carries a log sequence number (LSN) and an operation code. 1 is a delete, 2 is an insert, 3 is the row before an update and 4 is the row after. So an update adds two rows, per Microsoft's change table reference.

Two details trip up first-time readers. Don't order by `__$seqval`; use `__$command_id`, which orders changes inside a transaction. And Microsoft recommends calling the `cdc.fn_cdc_get_all_changes_` and `cdc.fn_cdc_get_net_changes_` functions instead of reading the change tables directly (reference).

Two SQL Server Agent jobs do the work, and their defaults matter. Microsoft's docs say the capture job runs continuously, handles up to 1,000 transactions per scan and waits 5 seconds between scans. The cleanup job runs daily at 2 A.M. and keeps entries for 4,320 minutes (3 days) (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > CDC or change tracking? Your first choice
text:
SQL Server ships two built-in ways to find changed rows. Microsoft's comparison page says change data capture reads the log after the fact and keeps history, while change tracking records changes as you write and keeps no history.

Change tracking notes that a row changed and gives its primary key (the column that uniquely identifies each row), but not the changed values. That's fine for the latest state, but no use for history.

Your edition can settle things fast. Microsoft's editions table lists change data capture as Yes for Enterprise and Standard, and No for Express (checked Oct 2026). Attaching a CDC database, or restoring it with the `KEEP_CDC` option, on an edition without CDC is blocked (Microsoft).

Azure SQL Database plays by different rules. Microsoft says a scheduler replaces the Agent jobs, and databases on the Database Transaction Unit (DTU) model need tier S3 or higher (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > How to turn CDC on
Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > How we picked
text:
We included maintained tools that document their SQL Server source in public, and looked at how each reads SQL Server, what the docs say about schema changes and retention, and where the data lands. We did not run the other tools; this is a documentation reading, not a lab test, and speed or reliability claims on vendor pages are the vendor's.

The order inside a group isn't a ranking.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Built into SQL Server
text:
**1. Native SQL Server CDC: best when the consumer is your own code**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: Agent jobs and change tables
- Lands data in: nowhere, you query it
- Price: part of the SQL Server editions that include it, which Microsoft's editions table (checked Oct 2026) lists as Enterprise and Standard

Native CDC is the base layer under most tools below, so it's worth knowing on its own. Microsoft's docs name the query functions that return changes over a range of LSNs.

What's good

- It needs no extra software and keeps history, with the values before and after each update, per Microsoft's change table reference.
- Microsoft says stopping the capture job loses no change data. It only pauses log scanning.
- Setting `@supports_net_changes` to 1 also generates a net changes function for the capture instance, and Microsoft's enable guide says that needs a primary key or unique index on the table.
- If an existing column changes data type, Microsoft says the change is propagated to the change table.
- On Amazon RDS, once you run `msdb.dbo.rds_cdc_enable_db`, AWS says any `db_owner` of the database can enable or disable CDC on its tables.

Where it falls short

- It only fills change tables (Microsoft), so you still need something to move the rows.
- Even in simple recovery mode, Microsoft says the log truncation point doesn't advance until captured changes are gathered, and `CHECKPOINT` won't truncate the log if the capture process isn't running while changes wait to be gathered. So a stopped capture job makes the log grow.
- Microsoft says both capture methods need SQL Server Agent running, and its editions table lists change data capture as Yes for Enterprise and Standard and No for Express (checked Oct 2026).
- Ask for a range that starts before the oldest kept change and Microsoft says there could be missing change data from aggressive cleanup. A range outside the valid window makes the query functions fail.
- New columns are ignored until you create a second capture instance, and Microsoft says a table can have at most two at once (checked Oct 2026).
- In a capture instance, Microsoft says computed columns always have a value of NULL, and by default a captured column can take at most 65,536 bytes (64 KB) in one INSERT, UPDATE, WRITETEXT or UPDATETEXT statement (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Run it yourself
text:
**2. Debezium: best for teams that already run Kafka**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: CDC change tables
- Lands data in: Kafka topics, one per table
- Price: free licence, per the Debezium licence page (checked Oct 2026); you pay for servers and staff

Debezium is an open-source CDC engine. Its SQL Server connector docs say it is based on the CDC feature in SQL Server 2016 Service Pack 1 and later, Standard or Enterprise edition (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- It takes a consistent snapshot first, then streams changes and picks up from the last log position after a restart (docs).
- Incremental snapshots copy a table in chunks (1,024 rows by default), and the SQL Server docs say they run alongside streaming and can resume after an interruption without losing data (checked Oct 2026).
- The docs say it can capture from an Always On read-only replica, though CDC must still be enabled on the primary node.
- The docs cover tuning the SQL Server capture job: a higher `pollinginterval` lowers the load on the database host and raises latency.
- The docs say its schema history provides the table structure in effect when a change event occurs.

Where it falls short

- Offsets are saved on a schedule, so after an outage the docs warn of duplicate events, so your loads must cope with repeats.
- The docs say SQL Server CDC isn't designed to store a complete history of changes, so the connector takes a snapshot to set a baseline.
- A table whose schema wasn't in the initial snapshot fails with a missing schema error. The documented fix starts with removing the schema history topic and clearing Kafka Connect offsets, and the docs say removing offsets should be done only by advanced users.
- The docs (checked Oct 2026) say it doesn't support schema changes while an incremental snapshot is running, and changing a primary key during one can cause incorrect results.
- Incremental snapshots need the connector to have permission to write to the signaling table (docs).
- `tasks.max` defaults to 1, and the docs say it can be raised to at most the number of entries in `database.names` (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Managed or vendor-run
text:
**3. Fivetran: best for teams that want a vendor to run SQL Server loads**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: change tracking, CDC, Binary Log Reader or Teleport Sync
- Lands data in: warehouses; Apache Iceberg through its Managed Data Lake Service
- Price: usage-based, billed on monthly active rows (checked Oct 2026), so the bill moves with how many rows change

Fivetran's SQL Server connector docs list four ways to find changes. Teleport Sync is the odd one out, because it skips SQL Server's change features and instead scans tables and compares row hashes between syncs. If a table has both change tracking and CDC on, Fivetran uses CDC.

What's good

- Its docs (checked Oct 2026) list four SQL Server methods and point to Teleport Sync when change tracking or CDC can't be enabled.
- Its connector docs cover SQL Server 2012 to 2025, with Binary Log Reader on 2016 to 2025 only (checked Oct 2026).
- Its docs say CDC data can be read from secondary replicas in an Always On availability group, but SQL Server doesn't allow CDC setup on a secondary, so all CDC setup happens on the primary node.
- With CDC, its docs say column type changes propagate automatically, and extra permissions let CDC track DDL changes without re-syncing the modified table.
- For change tracking, its docs say Fivetran detects when it couldn't process changes before they were deleted from the change table and triggers a re-sync of that table.
- Its docs say it supports the SaaS and Hybrid deployment models for all SQL Server implementations, and Hybrid needs an Enterprise or Business Critical plan (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Managed or vendor-run (part 2)
text:
- With CDC, Fivetran syncs only tables with a single capture instance, so a new column means a new instance and removing the old one (setup guide (checked Oct 2026)).
- Change tracking can't sync tables without a primary key or run on a replica (docs (checked Oct 2026)).
- With CDC, its docs say column type changes propagate but renamed columns, new tables and new columns do not.
- Iceberg goes through Managed Data Lake Service, a separate destination whose docs say it supports the SaaS deployment model (checked Oct 2026).
- That page also says Fivetran doesn't support position deletes for Iceberg tables, and on AWS the Glue catalog supports only one table per combination of schema and table names within a Region (checked Oct 2026).
- Under usage-based pricing, rollback syncs may fetch data from the previous month, and those past records count as new unique records toward monthly active rows for the current month (checked Oct 2026).

**4. Airbyte: best for self-run SQL Server loads on a schedule**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: CDC, in scheduled syncs
- Lands data in: warehouses and lakes; Apache Iceberg on S3 through its S3 Data Lake destination
- Price: Core is free to self-host, Cloud is paid (checked Oct 2026)

Airbyte's SQL Server docs say the connector uses SQL Server CDC with the transaction log, and CDC setup needs db_owner rights. Its CDC sync runs on a schedule, and Airbyte's CDC docs say it doesn't treat CDC sources as infinite streaming sources.

What's good

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Managed or vendor-run (part 3)
text:
- Core is free to self-host under the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2), which Airbyte's licensing summary says is restricted only for resale as a hosted service (checked Oct 2026). Beside CDC, the connector also has full refresh and incremental modes.
- Its SQL Server docs say the certified connector offers CDC using SQL Server's own CDC feature, for SQL Server 2016 Service Pack 1 and later (checked Oct 2026).
- Its S3 Data Lake docs say the connector writes Iceberg tables to S3 or S3-compatible storage using a REST, AWS Glue, Nessie or Polaris catalog, and that deduping is merge-on-read.
- The same S3 Data Lake page says it handles adding or removing a column, widening a column and changing the primary key. Because it never rewrites existing Iceberg data files, other schema changes are not handled.
- For truncate refreshes the S3 Data Lake connector writes to a staging branch and swaps it in at the end, so queries read the old version until then. It keeps the staging branch after a failed sync so a retry can recover.
- Its CDC docs say Airbyte adds metadata columns that begin with `_ab_cdc_` for CDC sources.

Where it falls short

- Incremental CDC needs a primary key, so tables without one get full refresh only (docs).
- Delivery is at least once (docs (checked Oct 2026)). CDC can't be enabled on tables with a clustered columnstore index (a storage layout built for analytics), and `hierarchyid` and `sql_variant` are not processed.
- Its CDC docs say changes made by TRUNCATE or ALTER will not appear in the logs and so not in the destination, and a refresh is required after any new table is added to a CDC connection.
- CDC syncs launch on a sync interval and read the logs up to the sync's start time (CDC docs). The first CDC sync takes a snapshot with a SELECT statement, which is effectively a full refresh.
- On the S3 Data Lake page, a Number-type primary key is stored as an Iceberg string, so ordering on it is lexicographic, and objects and unions are written as JSON strings.
- The same page cautions that if compaction runs at the same time as a truncate refresh sync, it deletes files from the current generation and causes data loss. It does not say who handles compaction.

**5. Estuary: best when you need to choose between CDC and change tracking**

At a glance

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Managed or vendor-run (part 4)
text:
- Reads SQL Server through: three connectors, CDC, change tracking or batch
- Lands data in: the destinations you choose, such as warehouses and lakes
- Price: not covered here

Estuary's SQL Server docs (checked Oct 2026) include a table of its three connectors. CDC is log-based and real time, and it handles tables without a primary key. Change tracking is real time too, stores only primary keys, and can capture computed columns, which CDC can't.

What's good

- Its docs set out the CDC versus change tracking tradeoff in a table, and say to use the batch connector for views or custom queries.
- The docs list three SQL Server connectors plus variants for Azure SQL Database, Amazon RDS and Google Cloud SQL, with setup steps for each platform. They say it is regularly tested against SQL Server 2017 and up (checked Oct 2026).
- The docs describe the CDC connector as log-based and real time, suited to full audit history and to tables without a primary key, but for those tables you set a key by hand in the collection definition.
- Change tracking is real time too, stores only primary keys for lower storage overhead on the source, and can capture computed columns, which CDC can't (docs (checked Oct 2026)).
- After a schema change, its docs say the connector detects a second capture instance and switches over once both are valid. An optional "Automatic Capture Instance Management" setting manages the instances for you.

Where it falls short

- CDC can read a replica, but the CDC worker must run on the primary. Change tracking doesn't support read replicas (docs (checked Oct 2026)).
- The batch connector polls, so expect latency of minutes to hours (docs).
- Its docs say a captured table should have a primary key, and without one you must specify a key manually in the Estuary collection definition.
- The docs (checked Oct 2026) say CDC cannot capture computed columns or computed primary keys, and change tracking may combine intermediate changes that happen in rapid succession.
- Automatic Capture Instance Management needs additional permissions (docs).
- Private and BYOC deployments need an annual plan and add fees based on the cloud infrastructure required. Its pricing docs publish no figure for those fees (checked Oct 2026).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Enterprise platforms
text:
**6. OLake Go: best for SQL Server changes into Iceberg or Parquet on your own storage**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: CDC capture instances, SQL Server 2017 or later
- Lands data in: Apache Iceberg or Parquet only
- Price: free licence, you pay for servers and staff

OLake Go is open source under Apache 2.0 (checked Oct 2026) and reads SQL Server in four sync modes: full refresh, full refresh plus CDC, CDC only, and full refresh plus incremental (see the SQL Server connector guide).

What's good

- The SQL Server connector guide lists parallel chunking, checkpointing and automatic resume for failed full loads. An optional `VIEW DATABASE STATE` grant (`VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE` on SQL Server 2022 or later) gives faster chunking for tables without a primary key.
- A "Manage Capture Instance" option creates new capture instances when schemas change, if the user has `db_owner` (see the guide).
- It can read from a read-only secondary replica with `ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly`, while CDC stays enabled on the primary. With Manage Capture Instance on, it asks for the primary's credentials so it can manage capture instances there (see the guide).
- It writes Iceberg tables to eleven catalog types, such as AWS Glue, REST, Polaris, Nessie and Unity (see the catalogs page), or Parquet files if you prefer.
- For Iceberg, a two-phase commit tracks per-chunk commit status in destination state, covering full refresh, incremental and CDC for MSSQL, to avoid inconsistencies and duplicate writes (see the v0.5.0 release notes).
- The guide gives the CDC enable commands for Amazon RDS and Google Cloud SQL, and the source supports SSL modes and SSH tunnels.

Good to know

- OLake Go is built for Iceberg and Parquet output, and you run it on your own infrastructure.
- Keep it reading inside the three-day change table window. Computed columns come through as `NULL`, and a clustered columnstore index blocks CDC, as it does in SQL Server itself.

Bottom line: Pick it if you want SQL Server changes in Iceberg tables on storage you own and can run a container. Snowflake, BigQuery and Redshift can still query the Iceberg tables it writes, depending on the catalog (see the compatibility page).

**7. Qlik Replicate: best for large mixed estates with an existing Qlik contract**

At a glance

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Enterprise platforms (part 2)
text:
- Reads SQL Server through: two source connection types (endpoints), a standard SQL Server endpoint and an MS-CDC endpoint
- Lands data in: the targets Qlik supports, listed in its support matrix
- Price: not published (checked Oct 2026)

What's good

- Qlik's MS-CDC endpoint docs say it reads Microsoft change tables instead of the log, which Qlik says lowers the risk of data loss from short log retention or unreachable log backups.
- The replication task turns on MS-CDC for the source tables for you, unless you'd rather do it by hand.
- The same endpoint can also be used to replicate from an Amazon RDS for SQL Server source, per the endpoint docs.
- Its prerequisites page points to `sys.sp_cdc_change_job` and a small `@pollinginterval` value to reduce latency.
- Qlik's pricing page lists "Qlik Open Lakehouse with ingestion and adaptive optimization for Apache Iceberg" in the Standard edition of Qlik Talend Cloud (checked Oct 2026).

Where it falls short

- Prices aren't published, and the product is client-managed software, so you run the server (checked Oct 2026).
- The prerequisites page says the CT table names must use the default `<SchemaName>_<TableName>_CT` format and the CT table must include the listed columns.
- The MS-CDC capture and cleanup jobs must be running (prerequisites).
- Microsoft ODBC Driver 18.5 must be installed on the Replicate machine, on Windows or Linux (prerequisites) (checked Oct 2026).
- On the pricing page, log-based CDC first appears in the Standard edition list for Qlik Talend Cloud, not in Starter (checked Oct 2026).

**8. Striim: best for log-backup reading and low load on the source**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: MS SQL Reader (CDC tables) or MSJet (log backups)
- Lands data in: many targets; Iceberg on Google Cloud Storage or S3 Tables
- Price: contact sales, with a Developer tier (checked Oct 2026)

Striim's SQL Server page says MSJet has higher throughput and lower use of the source server's compute, memory and disk than MS SQL Reader (Striim's claim, which we did not test). MS SQL Reader supports older SQL Server versions and more cloud SQL databases.

What's good

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Enterprise platforms (part 3)
text:
- You can pick the reader per source: MS SQL Reader for CDC tables, or MSJet for log backups (docs).
- Its Iceberg Writer docs list two write modes, Merge and Append Only, and say it propagates DDL changes from supported sources to the Iceberg tables.
- Its S3 Tables Writer docs list APPENDONLY and MERGE modes, with an Optimized Merge option for partial-image CDC, and DDL propagation for supported source operations.
- The SQL Server docs say Striim provides wizards for creating applications that read from SQL Server and write to various targets.
- Its pricing page lists a self-managed Striim Platform with clustered deployments with HA, and Striim Cloud with dedicated compute and networking.

Where it falls short

- MSJet reads log backups on disk, and the docs say backups on tape, virtual devices, mirror backups or Azure Storage aren't supported (checked Oct 2026).
- Its Iceberg Writer is Google Cloud Storage only; S3 Tables has its own writer (checked Oct 2026).
- The Iceberg Writer needs a compute engine and a catalog: Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Spark and a Lakehouse, Nessie or Polaris catalog (docs).
- With the Iceberg Writer, partitioned tables need manual table creation, and time source data types are written as strings (docs).
- The S3 Tables Writer uses Amazon EMR as the compute engine, and S3 Tables requires lowercase table, namespace and column names, which breaks wildcard mappings against uppercase-identifier sources.
- Both Iceberg writers recover on restart with at-least-once processing (Iceberg Writer, S3 Tables Writer).

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Cloud services
text:
**9. AWS Database Migration Service (DMS): best for AWS-centered teams**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: MS-Replication and MS-CDC
- Lands data in: AWS stores such as S3; the target list names S3, Kinesis, Kafka and others, and not Apache Iceberg
- Price: not covered here

DMS uses two methods, per its SQL Server CDC docs (checked Oct 2026). On a self-managed server, it uses MS-Replication for tables with primary keys and MS-CDC for tables without. Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for SQL Server doesn't support MS-Replication, so DMS uses MS-CDC for all tables there.

What's good

- AWS operates it, and the docs cover set-up with and without the sysadmin role.
- Its overview says you can run one-time migrations or replicate ongoing changes to keep sources and targets in sync.
- DMS version 3.4.7 and later can set up MS-CDC for the database and all tables automatically, if you are not using a read-only replica (CDC docs) (checked Oct 2026).
- Version 3.5.3 adds reading from log backups of Amazon RDS for SQL Server, per the CDC docs, and Kerberos authentication for SQL Server sources, per the source docs (checked Oct 2026).
- The source docs say it supports named instances of SQL Server and can use SSL between the endpoint and the replication instance.

Where it falls short

- The target list names S3, Kinesis, Kafka and others, and not Iceberg, so Iceberg tables from DMS output would need a step you add.
- Self-managed sources need a distribution database for MS-Replication (docs). That's extra set-up work.
- The source docs (checked Oct 2026) say columnstore indexes, memory-optimized tables, temporal tables, sparse columns and column-level encryption are not supported, and neither is replication from databases with accelerated database recovery (ADR) turned on.
- Per the source docs (checked Oct 2026), changes to computed fields aren't replicated, truncate commands aren't captured, and renaming tables or columns with `sp_rename` isn't supported.
- If the database is set up for neither MS-Replication nor MS-CDC, per AWS, tables without a primary key capture only INSERT and DELETE events; UPDATE and TRUNCATE events are ignored.
- The source docs say you may lose events if SQL Server archives them from the active transaction log to the backup log, or truncates them from it.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Cloud services (part 2)
text:
**10. Google Cloud Datastream: best for Google Cloud teams that want BigQuery or Cloud Storage**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: change tables or transaction logs, your choice per stream
- Lands data in: BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Apache Iceberg tables in BigQuery, with the data in your own buckets
- Price: not covered here

Datastream's SQL Server page lists self-managed servers (Enterprise 2008 and later, Standard 2016 Service Pack 1 and later), Amazon RDS, Cloud SQL and Azure SQL Database. For Cloud SQL, Express is not supported (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Datastream documents two methods per stream (checked Oct 2026). Change tables have fewer limits and no risk that log truncation fails a stream for good, at lower throughput, while the transaction logs method is faster and needs fewer resources.
- The docs (checked Oct 2026) say the change tables method supports replication of encrypted tables, which the transaction logs method does not (it can't handle Transparent Data Encryption).
- With the `enable_ddl_support_for_ct` label, Datastream checks`cdc.ddl_history` every five minutes and, when a column is added, creates a new capture instance, reads the old one up to the change, then reads the new one. You still delete the original instance afterwards, since SQL Server allows two per table.
- Datastream replicates user-defined data types, but stores the base data type they derive from in the destination.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Cloud services (part 3)
text:
- The transaction logs method doesn't support Transparent Data Encryption or column-level encryption (that data becomes `NULL`), and doesn't replicate columns added after a stream is created (docs (checked Oct 2026)).
- Streams are limited to 10,000 tables, and a table with more than 500 million rows can't be backfilled unless it has a unique index with no nullable columns, all included in the stream (checked Oct 2026).
- Its Iceberg tables in BigQuery are append-only, and the page does not mention Amazon S3.
- `SQL_VARIANT`, `HIERARCHYID`, `GEOMETRY` and `GEOGRAPHY` columns aren't replicated (docs).
- Databases with delayed durability or accelerated database recovery (ADR) enabled aren't supported, and neither is Windows Active Directory authentication (docs (checked Oct 2026)).
- With the change tables method, dropping a column replaces its data with `NULL`, and renaming columns isn't supported when CDC is enabled (docs (checked Oct 2026)).

**11. Microsoft Fabric mirroring: best for teams whose target is Microsoft Fabric**

At a glance

- Reads SQL Server through: CDC (SQL Server 2016 to 2022) or change feed (2025)
- Lands data in: Microsoft Fabric OneLake
- Price: replication compute is free, per Microsoft (checked Oct 2026); queries use Fabric capacity, so check what that costs you

Fabric mirroring copies a SQL Server database into Fabric. Data lands in OneLake as Delta tables, which Microsoft says now include virtual Iceberg metadata. Microsoft's limits page says mirroring of SQL Server 2016 to 2022 requires CDC, while SQL Server 2025 uses a different change feed (checked Oct 2026).

What's good

- Microsoft's docs say that for SQL Server 2016 to 2022 it reuses CDC if it's already on, or can set it up.
- The mirroring page lists SQL Server on Windows (Standard, Enterprise and Developer), Linux from 2017 CU18, and instances hosted on-premises, on an Azure VM or on non-Azure clouds for 2016 to 2022 (checked Oct 2026).
- Each mirrored database gets an autogenerated SQL analytics endpoint, a read-only copy you can query with T-SQL (docs).
- To mirror a server behind a firewall, the docs say to set up an on-premises data gateway or a virtual network data gateway.
- If CDC isn't on, the limits page (checked Oct 2026) says the tutorial makes `fabric_login` a temporary member of the sysadmin server role to configure it.

Where it falls short

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > The 11 best SQL Server CDC tools > Cloud services (part 4)
text:
- Microsoft says you can't mirror a SQL Server 2025 database that has CDC enabled (limits page (checked Oct 2026)). SQL Server 2025 mirroring also needs Azure Arc and isn't supported on Linux or on an Azure VM.
- A schema change breaks mirroring on 2016 to 2022 until you re-enable CDC for the table, and it restarts a full snapshot on 2025 (limits page (checked Oct 2026)).
- Per the limits page (checked Oct 2026), mirroring works only on a primary database of an availability group, doesn't support a failover cluster instance, and can't mirror a database already mirrored in another Fabric workspace.
- You can mirror up to 1,000 tables, and the limits page says tables above that are not replicated (checked Oct 2026).
- On the limits page, clustered columnstore indexes aren't supported, tables using temporal history, Always Encrypted, in-memory, graph or external features can't be mirrored, and LOB columns over 1 MB are truncated to 1 MB (checked Oct 2026).
- Active transactions hold log truncation until the mirror catches up, and Microsoft says to monitor the source transaction log so it doesn't fill.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > What actually breaks SQL Server CDC
text:
The diagram shows the three failures that stop a pipeline outright. A fourth, large columns, corrupts data quietly.

The Agent stops.Microsoft says both capture methods need SQL Server Agent running. No Agent, no changes.

The tool is down longer than retention. The default is three days, which sounds fine until a long weekend. Fivetran's docs recommend seven days and, for change tracking, say it triggers a re-sync of a table when changes were deleted before it could process them. Microsoft says a request for a range outside the valid window fails or can miss data.

A column is added.Microsoft says new columns are ignored unless you create a second capture instance. A dropped column gets `NULL` (no value). Microsoft's `sp_cdc_enable_table` page (checked Oct 2026) says a source table can have at most two capture instances.

Large columns come through empty.Microsoft says`varchar(max)`, `nvarchar(max)` and `varbinary(max)` columns are NULL on update rows unless the column changed in that update. Columns of type `text`, `image` and `ntext` are NULL on delete and update rows. A loader that treats NULL as "set to empty" will overwrite good data.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > What actually breaks SQL Server CDC > A schema change, step by step
text:
Microsoft's fix for a new column is a second capture instance, with a new name, that has the new shape.

sql

```
EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table @source_schema = 'dbo', @source_name = 'my_table',
  @role_name = 'my_role', @capture_instance = 'dbo_my_table_v2';
```

Tools that overlap instances. Estuary (docs) and OLake Go (guide) say they detect the second instance and switch when both are valid. Wait for your tool to confirm the switch before you delete the old instance.

Tools that expect one instance. Fivetran only supports tables with a single capture instance, so its setup guide (checked Oct 2026) tells you to create the new instance and delete the old one. Its connector page adds in its feature table that CDC tracks schema changes by re-syncing the modified table, unless you grant extra permissions.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > What actually breaks SQL Server CDC > A check to run before every restart
text:
Microsoft says the query functions fail if your range is outside the valid window, so compare your tool's saved position with the oldest and newest positions SQL Server still holds.

sql

```
SELECT sys.fn_cdc_get_min_lsn('dbo_my_table') AS oldest_lsn,
       sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn()               AS newest_lsn;
```

Debezium keeps its position as an LSN in its offsets. If your saved position is older than `oldest_lsn`, cleanup has already removed changes you never read.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > A worked selection case
text:
The case below is invented to show the method, and we did not run the other tools.

Suppose a SQL Server 2022 Standard edition server has 300 tables. Twenty have no primary key, two have a clustered columnstore index, and the target is Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3. Schemas change about monthly.

| Requirement | Fits | Does not fit, and why |
| Twenty tables without a key | Estuary CDC ( docs ), AWS DMS (MS-CDC) ( docs ), Fivetran CDC ( docs ) | Airbyte CDC copies those tables by full refresh only ( docs ); Fivetran change tracking skips them ( docs ) |
| Two columnstore tables | Fivetran Teleport Sync, which its docs point to when CDC can't be enabled | CDC tools for those two tables, since Microsoft says (checked Oct 2026) CDC can't be enabled on a clustered columnstore index |
| Iceberg on S3 | Fivetran Managed Data Lake Service , Airbyte S3 Data Lake , OLake Go | Datastream (Iceberg tables in BigQuery, docs ), Striim (Google Cloud Storage or Amazon S3 Tables, not plain S3, per its Iceberg Writer and S3 Tables Writer docs), Fabric mirroring (lands in OneLake, docs ), AWS DMS (its target list does not name Iceberg) |
| Monthly schema changes | Estuary and OLake Go (switch to a second instance) | Fivetran needs a new capture instance each time ( setup guide (checked Oct 2026)) |

No single tool covers every row, so each path needs a compromise.

Airbyte can do CDC for tables with keys and full refresh for the rest. OLake Go covers the ordinary tables with CDC, and its guide describes full refresh chunking for tables without a primary key.

If two rows fit, shortlist both and test them.

title: Compare: Best SQL Server CDC Tools in 2026, Compared | OLake > So which tool should you pick? > Which SQL Server CDC tool fits you?
text:
Question 1 of 6

Who should run the pipeline?

FAQ
Q1. What is SQL Server CDC?

SQL Server's built-in way to record inserts, updates and deletes on a table, using Agent jobs that read the transaction log into change tables.

Q2. Does SQL Server CDC need SQL Server Agent?

Yes, on SQL Server and Azure SQL Managed Instance, per Microsoft. Azure SQL Database skips the Agent and uses a scheduler instead, per Microsoft.

Q3. What is the difference between CDC and change tracking?

CDC reads the log and keeps changed values and history. Change tracking only notes that a row changed, plus its primary key, with no history.

Q4. How long does SQL Server keep CDC changes?

Three days by default (4,320 minutes), per Microsoft (checked Oct 2026). You can change the value with sys.sp_cdc_change_job.

Q5. What happens to CDC when I add a column?

New columns are ignored by the current capture instance, per Microsoft. Create a second instance with the new shape, switch the tool to it, then remove the old one.

Q6. Can I send SQL Server changes to Apache Iceberg?

With some tools. Fivetran and Airbyte document Iceberg destinations, Datastream writes Iceberg tables in BigQuery with data in your own buckets, and Striim writes to Google Cloud Storage or Amazon S3 Tables. The AWS DMS target list names S3, Kinesis, Kafka and others, and not Iceberg.

Q7. What permissions do I need to enable SQL Server CDC?

sysadmin to enable CDC on a database, then db_owner for each table, per Microsoft. On Amazon RDS you run msdb.dbo.rds_cdc_enable_db instead, per AWS.
