title: GitHub issue olake#1242: kafka discover: ProduceSchema discards fetch and schema-resolution errors, silently producing an empty or partial schema
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ProduceSchema` drops errors at two levels, so a topic whose messages could not be fetched or resolved is reported as a successfully-discovered stream with a missing or incomplete schema.

## The path

In `drivers/kafka/internal/kafka.go:249-265`:

```go
_ = k.processKafkaMessages(ctx, reader, func(record types.KafkaRecord) (bool, error) {
    messageCount++
    if record.Data != nil {
        mu.Lock()
        err := typeutils.Resolve(stream, record.Data)
        mu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
            return true, err   // (a) propagated to processKafkaMessages...
        }
    }
    shouldExit := messageCount >= 10000 || record.Message.Offset >= endOffset.Offset-1
    return shouldExit, nil
})
return nil                      // (b) ...and then thrown away here
```

- **(a) → (b)**: `typeutils.Resolve` failures are returned from the callback, `processKafkaMessages` propagates them, and the `_ =` assignment discards the result.
- The per-partition closure then unconditionally `return nil`, so `utils.Concurrent` sees every partition as successful and the `if err != nil` check at line 267 can never fire for these causes.
- The same discard hides fetch-side failures: `processKafkaMessages` wraps genuine fetch errors as `constants.ErrNonRetryable` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:271-273`), and those are discarded too.

## Impact

Discover reports success for a topic it could not actually read. The resulting stream has no resolved columns beyond the `_kafka_*`…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Discover samples the first 10,000 messages to infer the stream schema. Columns that appear later are handled by schema evolution during sync, so a partial sample does not block the pipeline. Non-JSON messages are skipped during sampling. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

title: GitHub issue olake#1241: kafka: ReaderManager.exitMode is never reset and is shared by all readers, so one rebalance halts every reader for the rest of the sync
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`ReaderManager.exitMode` (`pkg/kafka/types.go:41`) is a single `atomic.Int32` on the manager, shared by every reader in the group. Two problems follow from that.

### 1. It is never reset

`exitMode` is only ever written to a *terminal* value — `gracefulExit` or `nonRetryableExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:316`, `pkg/kafka/reader.go:323`). Nothing ever stores `normalProcessing` back. `RestartReader` recreates the franz-go client but leaves `exitMode` untouched (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:273-292`).

So once any rebalance fires, every subsequent retry attempt short-circuits immediately: `processKafkaMessages` checks `FetchExitState()` before its first poll (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`) and returns straight away. The retry driven by `RetryOnBackoff` (`utils/utils.go:482`) burns its attempts without ever reading a record.

### 2. It is global, not per-reader

The driver runs readers in parallel — `ChangeStreamConfig` returns `parallel=true` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:24-26`), and `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:82` fans out one goroutine per reader index. All of them share one `ReaderManager` and therefore one `exitMode`.

A rebalance callback on **one** reader sets the flag for **all** of them. Readers that still hold valid, unaffected partition assignments stop mid-partition too. Combined with issue #1240 (graceful exit reported as success → offsets committed), a single rebalance on one reader can cause short reads to be committed across every partition in the sync…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama Sharing exitMode across readers, and not resetting it after a rebalance, is by design.

When a rebalance is detected, we gracefully stop the sync. At that point, all readers need to stop consuming further records; otherwise, there is a risk of duplicate processing because their partition assignments may no longer be valid.

During the retry, static membership prevents another rebalance from being triggered. As a result, the exit mode is not changed back at that point, and the readers continue with the existing exit state.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

title: GitHub issue olake#1240: kafka: graceful rebalance exit is reported as success, committing offsets for partitions that were never fully read
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

When a consumer group rebalance is detected mid-sync, the Kafka driver stops processing and reports **success**, which causes `PostCDC` to commit offsets. Because the partitions were only partially consumed, the unread remainder is skipped permanently on the next run.

## The path

1. `kgo.OnPartitionsAssigned` / `OnPartitionsRevoked` fire → `r.exitMode.Store(gracefulExit)` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:312-318`).
2. `FetchExitState()` returns `(stop=true, err=nil)` for `gracefulExit` (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:359-361`).
3. `processKafkaMessages` sees `stopProcessing==true, err==nil` and returns `nil` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:250-252`).
4. `StreamChanges` gets `err == nil`, so it skips the error return and proceeds to build `metadataByStream` from whatever landed in `lastMessages` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:146-171`).
5. `streamChanges` in `drivers/abstract/cdc.go:107-111` runs the deferred `PostCDC` — which calls `reader.CommitRecords(ctx, messages...)` (`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go:218`).

The committed offset is the last record processed *before the rebalance interrupted us*, not the partition end offset. On the next sync `PartitionsForStream` skips everything at or below that committed offset (`pkg/kafka/reader.go:139-142`), so the records between the interrupt point and `EndOffset` are never read.

A rebalance is a normal, expected event (a member joining/leaving, a session timeout, a coordinator move). Treating it as a clean completion turns a routine even…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama The statement that the records between the interruption point and `EndOffset` are never read is not correct. The committed offset is intentionally the last successfully processed record before the rebalance, rather than the partition's `EndOffset`.

On the next sync, `PartitionsForStream` resumes from the committed offset, so records after the interruption point are still consumed. We also emit a `Warnf` log when the sync is stopped gracefully.

This behavior is intentional and ensures that rebalances are handled safely without data loss.

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

title: GitHub issue olake#1239: kafka source: Avro/Protobuf wire-format messages silently mis-decoded as JSON when schema_registry is not configured
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

`drivers/kafka/internal/cdc.go` `parseKafkaData`/`parseData` detects Confluent wire-format messages (`isConfluentWireFormat`, magic byte `0x00` + 4-byte schema ID) but when `schema_registry` is not configured, it unconditionally treats the payload as JSON:

```go
if isConfluentWireFormat(data) {
    if k.schemaRegistryClient == nil {
        return decodeJSONMessage(data[5:])
    }
    ...
```

If the topic actually contains Avro- or Protobuf-encoded data (which is the common case when wire-format framing is present at all — plain JSON producers rarely emit the magic byte), this attempts to JSON-decode raw binary Avro/Protobuf bytes. Best case this fails with a confusing `invalid character ...` JSON parse error that gives no hint that a schema registry is required; worst case (rare, if the binary happens to start with valid JSON-parseable bytes) it could produce garbage decoded data silently, which is worse than a clean failure.

Yes, a Kafka source can be configured today without `schema_registry` (`Config.SchemaRegistry *kafka.SchemaRegistryClient` is optional and `Validate()` only checks it when non-nil, see `drivers/kafka/internal/config.go:62-66`). That's a legitimate mode for JSON topics without wire-format framing — this issue is only about the case where wire-format framing IS detected but no registry is present to resolve it.

## Suggested fix

When `isConfluentWireFormat(data)` is true and `k.schemaRegistryClient == nil`, return a clear, actionable error…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @maltzsama thanks for flagging this. We are looking into it and will get back shortly.

- collaborator: @maltzsama  treating Confluent-framed messages as JSON when schema_registry is not configured is by design. We cannot reliably determine whether a message is JSON or Avro just by looking at the message, since JSON does not have a fixed schema. We use sampling to infer the JSON schema, and this behavior was implemented accordingly. Could you let us know if this has caused any problems on your side?

- collaborator: Closing this issue due to inactivity. Please feel free to reopen it if it's still relevant or if further work is needed.

title: GitHub issue olake#1200: feat(MySQL): parse DDL and apply it in stream order, instead of dropping every cached table
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem

`isDDL` matches a `QueryEvent` with a regex, and `invalidate()` drops **every** cached table's column metadata. So:

- A gh-ost/pt-osc run on a table we do not capture, or routine partition maintenance, evicts every active stream. Each reloads from `information_schema` on its next row event.
- A reload only ever returns the *latest* schema. In a backlog with two or more DDLs on one captured table, the reload after the first gives the schema after the last, so the rows in between decode wrong.

A regex cannot fix either — it never learns which table the statement touched. `RENAME` and `DROP` take table lists, and the gh-ost cutover swap (`RENAME TABLE users TO _users_del, _users_gho TO users`) must not be attributed to its first name alone.

## Proposed fix

Replace `invalidate()` with an `applyDDL` that parses the statement and advances each cached `tableMeta` in stream order:

- `ast.AlterTableStmt` on a cached table → mutate `tableMeta.Columns` in place, honouring `FIRST`/`AFTER`, then set `AnchoredAt` to the DDL's position.
- `ast.RenameTableStmt` / `ast.DropTableStmt` → drop only the named entries, walking every pair so the cutover swap is handled.
- `ast.CreateTableStmt` → drop the named entry, for MariaDB's `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`.
- Index, constraint, partition, table option, DML → ignored. **No eviction.**
- Parse error, or an alteration naming a column we do not have → today's drop-all, or fail the run naming the table and statement. Never guess.

## No…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Closing this as the fix is merged in https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/1298

title: GitHub issue olake#1189: arrow_writes: true breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE
text:
Issue (completed): **Title:** `arrow_writes: true` breaks CDC deduplication on Iceberg/Glue destination — no equality-delete written, rows physically duplicate on every UPDATE

## Environment
- OLake UI: v0.5.0 (`olakego/ui`)
- OLake worker: v0.3.10 (`olakego/ui-worker`)
- Source connector: `olakego/source-mysql:v0.9.5`
- Source: MySQL 8.0 (Aurora MySQL 3.10), CDC via binlog (`ROW`, `FULL` row image, GTID on)
- Destination: Iceberg via Glue catalog, S3 storage
- Deployment: official `docker-compose.yaml` from the OLake repo, minimal profile (no Fusion/Amoro optimizer running)

## Summary
With the destination config `writer.arrow_writes: true`, any row that receives more than one CDC event in short succession (e.g. an application `INSERT` immediately followed by an `UPDATE`, a very common pattern — create a record, then fill in a few more fields moments later) gets written as **two separate physical rows** in the Iceberg table, with **no equality-delete file ever produced** to mark the older version as superseded. A plain `SELECT * FROM table` returns both versions forever. Setting `writer.arrow_writes: false` (Legacy writer) on an otherwise identical destination fixes this completely.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a MySQL source with `sync_mode: strict_cdc` (or `cdc`) on a table with `source_defined_primary_key: ["id"]`, `default_stream_properties.append_mode: false`.
2. Configure an Iceberg/Glue destination with `arrow_writes: true`.
3. Let the sync run against a table that receives real…

title: GitHub issue olake#1188: Iceberg legacy writer truncates timestamptz precision from microseconds to milliseconds

title: GitHub issue olake#1177: Iceberg destination: selected_columns excludes OLake metadata columns from CREATE-time schema, breaking _olake_id identifier field
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- Olake version: v0.9.5 (also present on current `master` as of this report)
- Destination: Iceberg, REST catalog (AWS S3 Tables)
- Source: Postgres, CDC (pgoutput)

## Description

When a stream's `selected_columns.columns` is a non-empty allowlist, the Iceberg destination excludes OLake's own metadata columns (`_olake_id`, `_olake_timestamp`, `_op_type`, `_cdc_timestamp`) from the schema sent to the writer at `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` time, because they are never listed in the user's column allowlist. The table therefore gets created (or evolved) without `_olake_id`, with no identifier field at all.

Once real records are written, `_olake_id` (and the other three metadata columns) get merged into the row data regardless of `selected_columns` (`destination/iceberg/iceberg.go`, `FlattenAndCleanData`: `maps.Copy(records[idx].Data, record.OlakeColumns)`), so `_olake_id` shows up as a "new column" against the table's actual schema. Schema evolution then adds it as a new field on an existing table, and Iceberg requires new fields on an existing table to be optional. Right after that, OLake calls `UpdateSchema.setIdentifierFields(["_olake_id"])`, which throws:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot add field _olake_id as an identifier field: not a required field
	at org.apache.iceberg.Schema.validateIdentifierField(Schema.java:168)
```

This repeats on every retry (with backoff) because `GET_OR_CREATE_TABLE` loads the already-created, already-broken table rath…

- collaborator: Hi @erikcw , this has been fixed in v0.10.1 . Please check it and let us know if it fixes your problem.

title: GitHub issue olake#1175: Postgres CDC: unchanged TOAST values are lost should we read them back from the source?
text:
Issue (completed): ## TL;DR

When an `UPDATE` doesn't touch a large out-of-line (TOASTed) column, Postgres leaves that column out
of the WAL. OLake currently writes a placeholder string for such columns into the destination. One fix is to read the value back from the source through a held `REPEATABLE READ` transaction. **It works and it is provably correct, but we have measured what it costs and would like input before committing to it.** A second approach reconstructing the value from the destination is tracked in the companion issue and puts zero load on the source (here postgres database).

---

## 1. The problem

A tuple must fit in an 8 KB page. Postgres moves large variable-length values (`text`, `jsonb`,
`bytea`, …) into a companion TOAST table, leaving an 18-byte pointer behind. When you update a row
**without changing that column**, Postgres does not rewrite it, so there is nothing to put in the
WAL. Logical replication sends a marker instead:

> `Byte1('u')` "Identifies unchanged TOASTed value (the actual value is not sent)."
> [PostgreSQL protocol docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/protocol-logicalrep-message-formats.html)

This is exact, not a heuristic. The protocol tells us precisely which columns are affected.

### What OLake does today

`pkg/waljs/pgoutput.go` writes the literal string `__olake_unavailable_value__` into the column.

Before Postgres moves a value out of the row, **it tries to compress it first**. Only if the value is
*still* too large after compression does…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Closing in favor of #1176.
- Re-reading from the source needs a transaction held open for the whole CDC run, which stops vacuum from cleaning up.
- Measured on a busy source: 10× database growth, ~14× CPU per unit of work.
- OLake should not put extra load on the user's database.
- Unchanged TOAST values will be read back from the destination instead.

title: GitHub issue olake#1069: Postgres CDC cannot run against a read-replica: `pg_current_wal_lsn()` errors during recovery
text:
Issue (completed): ### What happens

Point the Postgres driver at a physical standby and every CDC run dies before any data moves:

```
failed to get slot position: ERROR: recovery is in progress (SQLSTATE 25006)
```

### Why

`pkg/waljs/replicator.go` builds the slot lookup with `pg_current_wal_lsn()`:

```go
ReplicationSlotTempl = "SELECT plugin, slot_type, confirmed_flush_lsn, pg_current_wal_lsn() as current_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name = '%s'"
```

That is a WAL control function, and it raises `recovery is in progress` on a standby. The standby equivalent is `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()`. Nothing branches on `pg_is_in_recovery()`, so there is no path through this that works on a replica.

`GetSlotPosition` runs from `Postgres.PreCDC` (`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go`) on every CDC run, and again in the LSN wait loop in `replicator.go`, so it fires immediately rather than partway through a sync.

### Why it matters

Postgres 16 added logical decoding on standbys, so the slot can live on a replica and keep decode load off a busy primary. The rest of the driver already looks compatible: `pg_replication_slot_advance()` is allowed on a standby for slots local to it, and `IdentifySystem` returns the replay position there. This one expression is the whole blocker.

The MSSQL driver picked up read-replica support in #949 and #991. This is the Postgres counterpart.

### Reproduction

PostgreSQL 18, a streaming replica built with `pg_basebackup -R`, `wal_level=logical` and `hot_standb…

title: GitHub issue olake#1014: Bug: Concurrent record filtering causes out-of-order data corruption
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
Concurrent filtering in `utils/typeutils/filter.go` scrambles record order. 
**Impact:** Processing CDC events out-of-order leads to data corruption (e.g., applying an older `UPDATE` after a newer one, or `DELETE` before `INSERT`).
## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a pipeline with a filter.
2. Ingest a batch of ordered records.
3. Observe the output from `FilterRecords`—the records are shuffled due to non-deterministic goroutine execution and mutex locking.
## Expected behavior
Filtered records must strictly retain their original sequence.
## Actual behavior
Records are appended to the `filtered` slice randomly as goroutines complete.
## Proposed Solution
Instead of appending directly via a mutex, either:
1. Process records sequentially (safest/simplest).
2. Concurrently evaluate conditions into an index-mapped boolean array, then sequentially build the final filtered slice.

Discussion:

- none: Evaluating predicates concurrently into an index-addressed result array and compacting in a second ordered pass preserves sequence without giving up parallel predicate work. The implementation should also define how a predicate error or panic affects the batch: cancel remaining workers and return no partial reordered output, rather than silently dropping an index. A deterministic test can insert per-record delays in reverse order and verify that surviving CDC records retain their original sequence across many runs.

This looks similar to the LOB/null column issue seen with AWS DMS. ## Environment - Source: PostgreSQL - Destination: S3 Parquet - Sync mode: CDC - Affected column type: `jsonb` - Example affected column: `invoice_details` ## Issue During CDC, the `jsonb` column becomes `null` in the destination Parquet files, even though the source PostgreSQL table contains non-null values. The affected `jsonb` values are relatively large. Most values in this column are around 3 KB to 15 KB. ## Expected behavior The `jsonb` column should be replicated correctly to S3 Parquet during CDC, preserving the original value from PostgreSQL. ## Actual behavior The `jsonb` column is written as `null` in the destination during CDC for affected rows. ## Impact This causes data loss in the destination because important JSON payloads are missing after CDC replication. Using append-only mode with query-side deduplication may work as a temporary workaround, but CDC mode should ideally preserve the full `jsonb` value. ## Questions 1. … Discussion: - collaborator: @Rtunc ,Thanks for reporting this issue and for the detailed investigation. Regarding your questions: 1. **Is there currently a size limit for jsonb / LOB columns in PostgreSQL CDC?** Large `jsonb` values can be affected during CDC because PostgreSQL WAL records may not contain the full value for TOASTed columns. In such cases, the column value may appear as `null` in the destination. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/storage-toast.html 2. **Could this be related to PostgreSQL TOASTed values?** Yes, this is related to PostgreSQL TOAST handling for large column values.

_What problem this feature is going to solve. Why this problem is important_

For the MSSQL connector which can connect to the read replica to replicate, capture instance management is disabled. This means that the automated create/delete of capture instances on the primary cannot work, like it would if connecting to the primary.

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf 

> What exactly UI does to stop job that is running?

In OLake, A Job is a Temporal workflow (a process). When you click **Cancel Run**, the UI sends a cancellation request to the workflow. Once the workflow context is cancelled, the workflow begins shutting down gracefully and the job is cancelled.

> If job is running with 10+ threads - how does it stop running query in every thread?

Since all the threads belong to the same workflow, when the workflow context is cancelled all the connections to the database instance from that workflow are closed. 

---

Also, could you please let us know which one of this are you facing:

1. The database query remains in the `EXECUTING` state even after the job is cancelled.
2. The job state in the OLake UI does not change to `CANCELLED` after clicking **Cancel Run**.
3. Both of the above.

title: GitHub issue olake#926: improvement: wire SIGINT/SIGTERM into root context for graceful shutdown
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem

OLake does not wire OS signals (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) into its root `context.Context`. When the operating system delivers a clean-shutdown signal — Kubernetes pod eviction, Karpenter node consolidation, `docker stop`, or Ctrl-C in a dev shell — the process exits immediately, without giving the CDC / backfill / destination-writer paths any chance to reach their existing `ctx.Done()` branches.

### Evidence

Searching the tree for any signal handling:

```
$ git grep -nE 'signal\.Notify|os\.Interrupt|syscall\.SIG(INT|TERM|HUP)' -- ':!LICENCE'
(no matches)
```

Confirmed on current `master` (`v0.6.5`).

The root command is built from cobra's default background context:

- `protocol/root.go` declares `RootCmd = &cobra.Command{...}` with no `SetContext` / `ExecuteContext` anywhere, so `cmd.Context()` inside every subcommand is `context.Background()` that never cancels on signals.
- `connector.go:18` — `protocol.CreateRootCommand(true, driver).Execute()` — uses plain `Execute()` (not `ExecuteContext`).
- `protocol/root.go:85` — `connector = abstract.NewAbstractDriver(RootCmd.Context(), ...)` — so `AbstractDriver.GlobalCtxGroup` / `GlobalConnGroup` are also rooted on a background context.

Meanwhile, the CDC / read paths already branch on `ctx.Done()` and would unwind cleanly if the context were cancellable:

- `pkg/waljs/pgoutput.go:47-108` — the pgoutput receive loop has `case <-ctx.Done(): return nil` as its top-level exit, and `ReceiveMessage` is called with a `conte…

title: GitHub issue olake#877: Job failed to run "Clear Destination" and stuck in "InProgress" state
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: Kubernetes using latest Helm chart
- **Olake version**:  0.4.1-0.5.1

## Description
If you add new table to the list of streams then  Olake runs "Clear Destination" for destination folder to remove any files in folder that will be used to store Parquet files for this new table. Its correct and expected, however if this API call to destination fails - then job stuck in "InProgress" state forever.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create destination with type Amazon S3 and point it to Google GCS bucket ( its compatible with S3 API)
2. Create job that will use this destination
3. Add  any table to the list of streams
4. Run sync, it should finish correctly
5. Add new table to the list of streams
6. You will see that "Clear Destination" job started. It generated error ( its expected)  and it stuck forever ( not expected)

Here is error message generated by worker
```
failed to clear destination: 
failed to drop the streams: 
failed to clear S3 files: 
failed to clear S3 prefix <source>/<table>: 
batch delete failed for filt Path <source>/<table>: 
BatchedDeleteIncomplete: 
some objects have failed to be deleted. caused by: 
failed to perform batch operation on "<source>/<table>/XYZ.parquet" to "tpt_olake": NotImplemented: 
A header or query you provided requested a function that is not implemented. status code: 400, request id: , 
host id: failed to perform batch operation on "<source>/<table>/XYZ.parquet" to "tpt_olake": NotImplemented: 
A header or…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @lkzcgfvf Since **clear-destination** is a destructive operation, we cannot allow it to fail in a partially completed state. In the event of an error, it should continue retrying indefinitely until the issue is resolved, ensuring consistency and preventing any half-applied changes. (This is an intended design decision)

In your case, as the clear-destination error is expected, we have an `api` to recover in-progress (failing) clear-destination operation. It cancels the `clear` operation and resumes the `sync` operation.

```bash
COOKIE_JAR="/tmp/olake.cookies"; trap 'rm -f "$COOKIE_JAR"' EXIT
curl --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/login' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"username":"admin","password":"password"}' \
  --cookie-jar "$COOKIE_JAR"

text:
curl -i --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/internal/project/123/jobs/<JOB_ID>/clear-destination/recover' \
  --cookie "$COOKIE_JAR"
```

> Note: Please update the hostname, port and the job_id as per your configuration. 

**If data is already present in the destination for the affected stream, It is recommended to drop the data manually before continuing with this process of recover**

- none: @vishalm0509 @vaibhav-datazip 
I agree that retry logic is very important for this operation, however  "continue retrying indefinitely" could be dangerous approach.
Job that stuck in "Running" state forever and it 
1. doesnt generate error
2. keeps running and do not allow to run itself next scheduled run

As result it will break pipeline and nobody will notice. In my particular case job was in this state ~18 hours, CDC pipeline was not collecting data from MySQL and we didnt know about it.

I would propose to adjust retry logic 
1. add logic that split errors in 2 categories: recoverable and  non-recoverable
2. add retry logic into recoverable errors ( network error, http 429, )
3. add configurable limits to retry logic ( ow many times to retry OR for how long)
4. stop work and exit with error for  non-recoverable error ( like AccessDenied OR  NotImplemented for DeleteObjects)

title: GitHub issue olake#862: AcknowledgeLSN times out when ClientXLogPos regresses behind confirmed_flush_lsn
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

`AcknowledgeLSN` in `pkg/waljs/replicator.go` times out with a fatal `"LSN not updated after 5 minutes"` error when `ClientXLogPos` is behind the replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`.

This happens in production when replicating databases with uneven WAL write/flush rates. We observed this on our OLake v0.5.0 deployment.

## Root Cause

There are two interacting issues:

**1. `ClientXLogPos` can regress behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`**

In `pgoutput.go:97` and `waljs.go:89`, the PrimaryKeepaliveMessage handler blindly assigns:

```go
p.socket.ClientXLogPos = pkm.ServerWALEnd
```

`ServerWALEnd` carries the WAL *flush* position, which can lag behind the WAL *write* position. Meanwhile, `PreCDC` advances the slot to `pg_current_wal_lsn()` (the write position). This creates a window where `ClientXLogPos` (flush) < `confirmed_flush_lsn` (advanced to write position).

**2. `AcknowledgeLSN` uses strict equality polling**

```go
if slot.LSN == walPosition {
    return nil
}
```

When `walPosition` (ClientXLogPos) is behind `confirmed_flush_lsn`, PostgreSQL silently ignores the StandbyStatusUpdate because `confirmed_flush_lsn` cannot move backwards. The equality check never matches, and the function times out after 5 minutes.

## Production Evidence

From our deployment logs:

```
state LSN:              E/D8EA31B8  (from pg_current_wal_lsn via PreCDC advance)
confirmed_flush_lsn:    E/D8EA31B8
IdentifySystem XLogPos: E/D8E19108  (flush position, 9MB behind)
keepali…

title: GitHub issue olake#856: implement 2pc in parquet writer (difficulty: hard) (part 2)
text:
- collaborator: @siiddhantt Thanks for sharing the design. Some clarification regarding where 2PC is needed: in OLake, 2PC is required across all sync modes, Initial Full Refresh, CDC, and Incremental, not just CDC/incremental backfill.
For CDC and Incremental syncs, the key requirement is that the state should be persisted at the same point as the destination commit (similar to the Iceberg implementation). This ensures that even if state file save fails afterward, the sync can safely resume from the last committed point in the destination without missing/duplicating the data, including for multi-stream jobs.
For Full Refresh as well, we still need commit tracking. The requirement there is to track which chunks have been successfully committed so resume after failure do not reprocess already committed chunks. 
To understand how this is handled in the Iceberg destination, you can also refer to this PR: https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/698
Please let us know if you run into any issues or if there are any design decisions you'd like to discuss further.

- contributor: Thanks for the clarification, @nayanj98 . I’ve updated the implementation direction accordingly.

The Parquet 2PC workplan now covers all three paths:
- Full Refresh: tracks committed chunk/thread IDs so retries can skip already committed chunks.
- Incremental: persists the destination-side cursor metadata at the same point as the Parquet commit.
- CDC: persists the committed LSN in destination metadata and recovers from it if the external state file is stale or was not saved.

I followed the Iceberg pattern from #698 for the state recovery contract, but now adapting it for Parquet by storing table-local metadata under `<namespace>/<table>/_olake_2pc/`, since Parquet does not have an Iceberg catalog commit layer. 
Then I'm also adding orphan cleanup for prepared-but-uncommitted Parq

title: GitHub issue olake#853: Bug: PostCDC write ordering causes irrecoverable LSN mismatch between OLake state and PostgreSQL replication slot
text:
Issue (completed): ## Bug Description

There is a write-ordering issue in `PostCDC` and `PreCDC` that causes OLake's persisted cursor (LSN) to advance **ahead** of the PostgreSQL replication slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`. Once this happens, the `validateGlobalState` check triggers a non-retryable error requiring a full "clear destination" — which is destructive and operationally painful for large datasets.

## Root Cause

In [`drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go:81-91`](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/main/drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go#L81-L91):

```go
func (p *Postgres) PostCDC(ctx context.Context, _ int) error {
    defer waljs.Cleanup(ctx, p.replicator.Socket())
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return ctx.Err()
    default:
        socket := p.replicator.Socket()
        p.state.SetGlobal(waljs.WALState{LSN: socket.ClientXLogPos.String()})  // ① writes to disk
        return waljs.AcknowledgeLSN(ctx, p.client, socket, false)              // ② tells PostgreSQL
    }
}
```

`SetGlobal()` calls `LogState()` which **synchronously writes the state file to disk** before `AcknowledgeLSN()` sends the `StandbyStatusUpdate` to PostgreSQL. If the process crashes, gets OOM-killed, or AcknowledgeLSN fails/times out between steps ① and ②:

- OLake's state file has LSN X (already flushed to disk)
- PostgreSQL's replication slot still has the old LSN Y (where Y < X)
- On restart, `validateGlobalState` detects the mismatch and returns a **non-retryable error**

The same pattern exists in …

Please add support for creating and managing OLake jobs from JSON (config-as-code), while keeping full parity in the UI for viewing, scheduling, and modifying those same jobs.

## Problem
Today, job setup is primarily UI-driven. For teams operating many pipelines/environments, we need:
- repeatable definitions in source control,
- promotion across dev/test/prod,
- reviewable diffs and change history,
- automation (CI/CD) for job creation/updates.

At the same time, operations teams still need UI workflows for monitoring and quick edits.

## Requested capability
1. Define/import job config via JSON (or YAML).
2. Jobs created from JSON appear in the UI like native jobs.
3. UI can:
   - view full config,
   - edit key fields,
   - manage schedule,
   - pause/resume/run-now.
4. Export existing UI jobs back to JSON.
5. Round-trip compatibility:
   - JSON -> UI -> JSON should be stable and predictable.

## Suggested UX/API
- `Create from JSON` action in Jobs page.
- `Export JSON` on each job.
- Optional API/CLI endpoints:
  - `POST /jobs` with JSON payload
  - `PUT /jobs/{id}` for updates
  - `GET /jobs/{id}/export` for canonical JSON

## Schema/versioning expectations
- Versioned schema (e.g., `schema_version`).
- Validation with clear field-level errors.
- Backward-compatible migrations when schema evolves.

## Scheduling expectations
- Schedule should be fully representable in JSON.
- UI schedule edits should update underlying JSON model.
- Timezone and cron handling …

- collaborator: @SeqNat Thank you for raising this feature request. We will definitely discuss on this internally and get back to you soon.

- contributor: @SeqNat we are closing this as its currently possible to do this via api call. (For OLake ui please visit localhost:8080/swagger). 
Also we are going to introduce bulk-edit feature in UI soon, so this would not be needed.

title: GitHub issue olake#848: Feature request: Continue job on per-table failure (skip_failed_tables) instead of failing entire sync
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem
In multi-table sync jobs, a single table failure currently causes the entire job to fail.  
For CDC migrations, this blocks throughput when only a subset of tables are problematic.

## Requested behavior
Add a job-level option to continue processing remaining tables when one table fails.

Example config intent:
- `skip_failed_tables: true` (or similar)
- On failure of table `X`, OLake marks `X` as failed, logs error details, and proceeds with table `Y`.

## Why this matters
- Large table sets often include a few edge-case tables (datatype/PK/chunking issues).
- We can still make progress on healthy tables while isolating blockers.
- This reduces rerun cycles and operational overhead.

## Expected output/observability
When enabled:
1. Per-table status in final summary:
   - `succeeded_tables`
   - `failed_tables`
   - `skipped_tables` (if applicable)
2. Exit code semantics:
   - Optional: non-zero only if all tables fail, or configurable strict mode.
3. Error report artifact:
   - machine-readable list (CSV/JSON) of failed tables + reason.

## Suggested config shape
```yaml
continue_on_table_error: true
max_table_failures: 0   # 0 = unlimited, or stop after N failures

Backward compatibility
Default should preserve current behavior (false / fail-fast) unless explicitly enabled.
Real-world use case
We are running CDC across many MSSQL tables; some tables fail due to connector edge cases (e.g., GUID boundary handling), but many others sync successfully.
A continue-on-…

title: GitHub issue olake#795: Unable to properly sort changes from MySQL Binlog  in Parquet file
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

I'm using MySQL 8.0.14 and running OLake in CDC mode with S3/Parquet as destination. In MySQL I start transaction, insert row and then update this row several times in the same transaction. After that I commit transaction and run OLake to get changes that I made. As result I get Parquet file which has all operations that I made ( c, u, u)  but with the same value in "_cdc_timestamp" column. I understand that "_cdc_timestamp" column represents commit timestamp and that is why all rows have the same values. But it means that there is no column that could be used to sort these rows in the same way as they were made in MySQL. They are properly sorted in Parquet file but after these Parquet files are loaded into datawarehouse for further processing there is no way to sort rows properly to get the latest version of row because most of datawarehouses don't guarantee you sort order during reading data from table.  As result its not possible to achieve correct results in pipeline that process rows from Parquet files.

## Steps to reproduce

title: GitHub issue olake#752: issue(postgres): check if tables selected in streams.json are subscribed in publication (part 2)
text:
what I changed :
## Problem
When a table is selected in `streams.json` but not added to the Postgres
publication slot, OLake either fails deep in WAL processing with a cryptic
error, or silently produces no CDC data for that table — giving the user
no indication of what's wrong.

## Solution
Added an explicit pre-flight check in `PreCDC` that queries
`pg_publication_tables` and compares the result against the selected streams.
If any table is missing, the sync fails **immediately** with a clear, actionable
error:
publication validation failed: the following tables are selected in streams.json
but are NOT tracked by publication "my_pub":
public.payments
Run: ALTER PUBLICATION my_pub ADD TABLE public.payments

- `drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go`: added `validatePublicationContainsStreams`,
  `checkStreamsInPublication`, `fetchPublicationTables` functions; called from `PreCDC`
- `drivers/postgres/internal/cdc_publication_test.go`: 10 table-driven unit tests
  covering happy path, missing tables, empty publication, case-insensitivity, etc.

title: GitHub issue olake#750: Add Structured Error Classification & Retry Strategy for Source Connectors
text:
Issue (completed): **Problem Statement**

Currently, errors raised by different source connectors (Postgres, MySQL, Kafka, Parquet, etc.) are handled inconsistently.
All failures are treated similarly, even though some errors are retryable (network, timeout) while others are fatal (schema mismatch, permission issues).

**This makes:**

Debugging difficult

Retries inefficient

Logs less actionable

Proposed Solution

Introduce a standard error classification and retry strategy across all connectors.

**Key Requirements:**

Define common error categories:

Retryable (network, transient failures)

Non-retryable (auth failure, invalid config)

Centralize error handling logic

Apply retry policies only where applicable

Improve error messages with context (source, stage, reason)

Ensure backward compatibility with existing connectors

Discussion:

title: GitHub issue olake#707: MySQL ENUM datatype doesnt work correctly in CDC mode
GitHub issue olake#706: fix: float values from binlog are not always same as the output of select * query of db
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

In MySQL, there can be a difference between the actual value stored in a column and the value displayed when running a `SELECT * FROM table` query.

For example, consider a `FLOAT` (float32) column in MySQL. A value inserted as `12345.678912345678` may be displayed as `12345.679` when queried using the MySQL CLI. This is due to MySQL’s default display formatting and rounding behavior for floating-point types.

However, when syncing this data using OLake’s Iceberg Writer or Parquet Writer, the value is captured as the actual stored value (`12345.678912345678`) rather than the rounded value shown in the MySQL CLI (`12345.679`).

This behavior should be corrected so that the synced data matches the value displayed by MySQL during a `SELECT` query, ensuring consistency between source reads and downstream data consumers.

---

https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/765752b2cae164eb5d73cef75365570ea8e22c4a/pkg/binlog/filter.go#L97-L101

---

###### This issue was generated by [todo-issue](https://github.com/DerJuulsn/todo-issue) based on a `TODO` comment in 765752b2cae164eb5d73cef75365570ea8e22c4a. It's been assigned to @badalprasadsingh because they committed the code.

Discussion:

- collaborator: hey @vimla01 , your understanding is mostly correct, but make sure you don't manually "interpret" the data. 

A good approach would be:

1. first, understand why the select * query from the source provides such an output
2. second, how OLake retrieves the value which was actually inserted, rather than the one displayed by the query
3. and then, you can move on with the implementation

Thanks for picking up the issue.

- contributor: Thanks for the clarification.. @badalprasadsingh 
From my understanding, MySQL FLOAT is stored as binary float32 ,while the value shown in SELECT is rounded for display. Binlog exposes a higher-precision float64 representation, which is why OLake currently retrieves extra precision.
I’ve implemented this by enforcing MySQL FLOAT (float32) semantics on binlog values, without any manual formatting or interpretation 
 I’ll raise the PR once I’m assigned/approved to proceed. @nayanj98 
Thanks.

title: GitHub issue olake#675: MariaDB Source Support
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

When trying to create a CDC task with a MariaDB RDS instance the version returned from Maria does not correlate to the appropriate MySQL version and the check within pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go returns the wrong command to determine whether CDC can be enabled on the task.

`query := utils.Ternary(majorVersion > 8 || (majorVersion == 8 && minorVersion >= 4), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew(), jdbc.MySQLMasterStatusQuery()).(string)`

In our example we are trying to connect to MariaDB 10.11.13 which returns the func `MySQLMasterStatusQueryNew` and not the supported command in func `MySQLMasterStatusQuery`. 

The error surfaced associated with this is `Query 1 ERROR at Line 1: : You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'LOG STATUS' at line 1`.

### Solution

Due to the compatibility between MariaDB and MySQL especially in the CDC space I wouldn't recommend cloning the driver and changing the version logic, I think the overhead there would be more than it's worth. 

The suggestion I had was to evaluate the Engine string within the pkg/jdbc/jdbc.go `MySQLVersion` function and resolve to the associated MariaDB version to MySQL for example in our instance:

MariaDB: `SELECT @@version` = 10.11.13-MariaDB-log

Within the `MySQLVersion` check for the string instance of `MariaDB` and if so present resolve to a MySQL version string. Ideally `10.11.13-MariaDB-log` would resolve to the `MySQLMas…

Discussion:

- collaborator: @jaytringfm We are picking this issue up internally and we will be releasing the fix in the coming versions. Thank you very much for getting this out here!

- collaborator: Hi @jaytringfm , 

A PR #677 has been raised to address this issue. The fix includes:

1. **MariaDB detection**: The code now properly detects MariaDB vs MySQL by checking the version string
2. **Query selection**: MariaDB will always use `SHOW MASTER STATUS` (the correct syntax) instead of `SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS`

This will be fixed in the next version of OLake once the PR is merged and released. You can upgrade to the new version to use MariaDB as a CDC source.

Thanks for reporting this issue!

title: GitHub issue olake#654: improvement: improve performance test by comparing RPS against average of last 5 runs instead of static benchmarks
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
Our current performance test uses hardcoded benchmark RPS values:
```go
// utils/testutils/test_utils.go
var benchmarks = map[constants.DriverType]benchmarkStats{
    constants.MySQL:    {Backfill: 15906.40, CDC: 15648.93},
    constants.Postgres: {Backfill: 12000, CDC: 1500},
    constants.Oracle:   {Backfill: 3500, CDC: 0},
    constants.MongoDB:  {Backfill: 0, CDC: 0},
}
```

During test execution, we check whether the current run’s RPS (from stats.json) is at least 90% of the static benchmark.
This approach is rigid and doesn’t adapt as performance evolves or hardware changes.

---

## Goal
Replace the static benchmark comparison with a dynamic benchmark calculated using the average RPS of the last 5 successful runs.

---
## Idea

1. Store the history of the last 5 RPS values for each driver + test type (Backfill & CDC).
2. On each new performance test run:
    - Load the last 5 historical RPS values for the given driver/test-type.  
    - Compute their average.
    - Compare the current RPS against 90% of that average.
3. Ensure that the test:
    - Falls back gracefully for the first few runs (e.g., <5 history entries).
    - Updates the history by adding the current run and removing the oldest entry.

---

## Checkbox

- [ ] Past 5 runs are persisted and readable during subsequent runs.
- [ ] Performance test compares current RPS with 90% of the average of those 5 runs.
- [ ] Logic supports both Backfill and CDC independently.
- [ ] No static hardcoded b…

We’re likely going to store the history as a JSON file and persist it using GitHub Actions artifacts (with max 90 day retention). This isn’t fully locked yet, but artifacts are the preferred direction for now.

For fallback when we have less than 5 entries, the idea is to keep it simple and avoid static benchmarks:

- **If there are 0 entries (first run)** → don’t fail the test, just record the RPS as the initial baseline.

- I**f there are 1–4 entries** → compute the average of what’s available and compare against 90% of that.

- **Once we have 5 entries** → use the rolling average of the last 5 runs.

Feel free to go through the current performance test code and propose an implementation along these lines (or a better one if you see fit). We can refine the exact behavior during review.

title: GitHub issue olake#525: bug: olake cdc fails to find new documents when connecting to sharded mongodb through mongos
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: docker
- **Olake version**:  for instance `0.2.3`
- **OS**: official olake docker image 
- **Mongo version**: 6

## Description

MongoDB change streams accessed through mongos (MongoDB router) have non-blocking behavior where cursor.TryNext() immediately returns false even when change events are available, causing Change Data Capture (CDC) operations to miss document changes. This occurs regardless of the number of shards behind mongos and is specific to the mongos routing layer. 

## Steps to reproduce

I created a sample project to demonstrate the issue. https://github.com/dschaaff/olake-monogs-cdc-bug-repro. The docker compose stack it contains sets up mongo behind mongos and contains a script to demonstrate the behavior.

- olake initial sync backfill
- write mongo document
- run olake and observe cdc does not pickup new document
- write mongo document
- run olake and observe cdc does not pickup new document

## Expected behavior

CDC successfully returns new documents when connecting through mongos. 

## Actual behavior

Olake never syncs new documents beyond the initial backfill.

The issue appears to be that the MongoDB Go driver's TryNext() method behaves differently when connecting through mongos vs. direct replica set connections:

  1. Direct Replica Set: TryNext() has blocking behavior
  2. Via Mongos: TryNext() is non-blocking and may return false immediately even when events exist

https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driv…

Discussion:

- contributor: @dschaaff we will fix it in next 2 days. Thank you for reporting.

- collaborator: Hi,

I’ve raised a PR implementing a PBRT-based resume token mechanism: https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/532

Could you please verify if this resolves your use case?

The issue occurs because, when connecting through mongos, the MongoDB Go driver’s non-blocking TryNext() can return false even when events exist. With the PBRT approach, we periodically checkpoint the latest stream position. These resume tokens are shard-safe, ensuring the CDC process reliably resumes without missing events.

- contributor: @vikash390 This change is working in my testing. CDC is correctly picking up changes from the sharded mongo setup now.

This can lead to runtime failures and a poor user experience due to misconfigurations. ### **Problems Identified** - No standardized validation framework for catalog-specific connection parameters.

title: GitHub issue olake#450: Backfill chunks use separate transactions, risking inconsistent cursor values during incremental syncs
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description
When running an incremental sync for the first time, Olake triggers a backfill before incremental to store initial cursor values.
Currently, in all drivers (Postgres, MySQL, Oracle), ChunkIterator opens a new transaction for each chunk.

This means that:
- Each SELECT * for a chunk runs under a different transaction.
- If new data is inserted/updated between chunk reads, incorrect chunk value is saved in state.
- The incremental sync may start from an incorrect cursor state.

Example scenario:
Backfill splits a table into 3 chunks with initial max cursor values:
```
Chunk 1: max cursor = 1  
Chunk 2: max cursor = 4  
Chunk 3: max cursor = 6  
```
While processing Chunk 2, some row from Chunk 1 changes so that its  max cursor is now 9, more changes happen in chunk 3 at same time so that its max cursor is now 10.
At the end of backfill, the saved cursor in state becomes 10 (the highest seen across all chunks).
Incremental sync will start from cursor >= 10, skipping rows that had cursor values between 6–9.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start a first-time incremental sync on a table.
2. Observe that in backfill.go, for each chunk, driver. ChunkIterator starts its own transaction.
3. While backfill is running, update data in the table between chunk queries (specially for the cursor fields set).

Result: final saved cursor value might be different than what it was supposed to be, which might result in some rows being skipped.

## Expected behavior

Backfill for a stream …

The Oracle driver currently lacks the functionality to provide sync progress statistics, such as an Estimated Time of Completion. This creates an inconsistent user experience compared to other drivers (e.g., MySQL, Postgres) where these stats are available.

Root Cause
The core issue is that the Oracle driver does not determine the total number of records to be synced before the process begins. As seen in the `oracle/backfill.go`, other drivers execute a query to get an approximate row count from the table's metadata and pass this value to the `AddRecordsToSyncStats` function.

Proposed Solution
We need to implement logic to query Oracle's data dictionary to get an estimated row count for the table being synced. Also, it needs to be near to accurate, so that it doesn't output wrong information.

For reference, Postgres and mysql driver's backfill code can be viewed.

title: GitHub issue olake#354: Enable Parallel Chunk Creation and Iteration to Improve Sync Performance
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

Currently, the chunking and iteration phases during the sync process are executed sequentially. First, all chunks for a table are created using a single database connection. Only after this phase is complete does the system begin iterating over and processing these chunks.

This design introduces two key limitations:

- Underutilization of database connections: While chunk creation is ongoing, only one database connection is used, regardless of the configured maximum.
- Slower sync performance: Since iteration waits for all chunks to be created, there is unnecessary delay.

### Solution

Introduce parallelization between chunk creation and chunk processing. The idea is to:

- Use one connection for chunk creation.
- As soon as a chunk is created, immediately hand it off to worker routines (using the remaining DB connections) for processing.
- Once all chunks are created, the initial chunking thread can also join the worker pool to help with remaining chunks.

This design will better utilize available DB connections and improve sync throughput by overlapping chunk creation and data extraction.

title: GitHub issue olake#278: [Feature] Add Configurable S3 Storage for Olake Runtime Artifacts
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem

Currently, Olake's sync process generates critical runtime artifacts such as `state.json`, which are essential for tracking sync progress and enabling resumption. These artifacts are stored only on the local filesystem where the Olake process is running.

This local-only storage presents several challenges:
1.  **State Loss & Difficult Resumption:** If the Olake process runs in an ephemeral environment (e.g., a Kubernetes pod that gets rescheduled, a temporary VM, or a CI runner) or if the local environment is lost, the state file is lost. This makes it impossible to reliably resume syncs from the last known point, potentially leading to data re-processing or data gaps.
2.  **Operational Complexity:** Managing state across distributed or dynamically provisioned instances becomes complex and error-prone.
3.  **Limited Debuggability & Auditing:** While not yet implemented for logs, the current architecture doesn't easily lend itself to persistently storing other artifacts like detailed logs, stats, or catalogs for long-term analysis, debugging across runs, or auditing.

This problem is important because robust state management and artifact persistence are crucial for:
*   **Data Integrity:** Ensuring syncs can be reliably resumed prevents data loss or duplication.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** Reduces manual intervention and re-processing time.
*   **Scalability & Resilience:** Enables Olake to run effectively in modern, distributed, and cloud-native environments…

text:
Issue (completed): **Description**:

There are a couple of improvements needed in the current config.json structure to enhance clarity and make configuration more intuitive:

**Issues Identified**:

1. default_mode is currently defined within the stream-specific properties of config.json, which is confusing. It should be part of catalog.json as a default sync mode applicable across streams.
2. The update_method field is vague and not self-explanatory, leading to confusion on its intended use and structure.

Move default_mode to catalog.json:
- Introduce default_mode as a top-level property in catalog.json.
- This value should apply to all streams unless a specific stream has its own override in the selected streams file.

- Introduce a required field inside it: sync_type, with possible values:
  - cdc
  - incremental/ full_refresh

If sync_type is set to cdc, the following sub-settings should be mandatory:
- replication_slot
- cdc_log_wait_time (renamed from the current initial_wait_time)

This change will bring clarity and modularity to the sync configuration, making it easier to manage and reason about both default and stream-specific behavior.

title: GitHub issue olake#192: urgent: create hash from all keys if primary key not present
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem
Currently, olake_id is being generated using the primary key fields of a record. However, in cases where the primary key is not present, this leads to all records getting the same olake_id, which is clearly undesirable and breaks uniqueness expectations.

## Proposed Solution:
When primary keys are not defined, generate olake_id by hashing all values in the record. This ensures a more consistent and unique identifier per row, even in the absence of a primary key.

This functionality is already available in the utility function utils.GetKeysHash(msg.Data, pkFields...) supports hashing record values. It simply needs to be used with the appropriate data when pkFields are empty or undefined.

## Action Items:

- Check if pkFields is empty

- If so, pass all record values to GetKeysHash

- Otherwise, continue using the primary key-based hashing as usual

title: GitHub issue olake#189: [Feat] Append-Only Write Mode
text:
Issue (completed): **Description:**
Implement an "Append-Only" write mode in OLake that appends (inserts) records into the target table instead of modifying or deleting existing records. This mode should introduce a dedicated column, OLAKE_OPERATION_TYPE, to indicate the type of operation performed. Users should have the ability to rename this column based on their preference.

**Current Behavior:**

- The current implementation only supports Soft Delete write mode via equality deletes.

**Proposed Behavior:**

- When enabled, all data modifications (inserts, updates, deletes) are appended as new records.
- A dedicated column, OLAKE_OPERATION_TYPE, is introduced to capture the type of operation.

The possible values for OLAKE_OPERATION_TYPE are:
- Insert: A new record inserted for the first time.
- Update: An update to an existing record, represented as a new row.
- Delete: A record that has been logically deleted, represented as a new row.
- Snapshot: A full snapshot of the table at a point in time.

Users can rename the OLAKE_OPERATION_TYPE column.

**Use Case:**

- Enables audit logging and historical tracking of changes without modifying existing records.
- Supports downstream processing for CDC (Change Data Capture) workloads.
- Helps maintain immutability for compliance or analytical purposes.

**Configuration Options:**
- Add an optional parameter (e.g., write_mode: append_only) to enable this feature.
- Allow customization of the OLAKE_OPERATION_TYPE column name.

Discussion:

- contributor: @rkhameshra any specific reason for this column to be renamable ?

- contributor: Just for user convenience, they might already have logs/events coming from current setup, easy to replace if system generated columns are renamable.

title: GitHub issue olake#151: improvement: Acknowledge Postgres LSN in batches
text:
Issue (completed): ## Problem
Currently, we only acknowledge the LSN after the entire sync is finished. While this works in many cases, it introduces a risk when the WAL logs are generated at a rate faster than we can read and process them.
If the assigned storage for WAL logs fills up before we finish syncing and acknowledge the final LSN, PostgreSQL might drop our cursor, leading to data loss or requiring a full resync.

## Proposed Solution:
- Acknowledge LSN in smaller batches during the sync process, not just at the end
- This allows PostgreSQL to safely drop older WAL logs in a timely manner
- Reduces pressure on WAL storage and provides more breathing room for the reader to keep up

https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/blob/ed705d25bc0cd1f048f2fa3e6309b3f55fb71b45/drivers/postgres/internal/cdc.go#L116-L121

Discussion:

- none: I will work on addressing this issue by implementing a solution to ensure that AcknowledgeLSN is called more efficiently.

Possible approaches to resolve this:
1. Track the number of records processed in each batch and trigger AcknowledgeLSN once a certain batch size is reached.
2. Introduce a buffering mechanism that accumulates records and acknowledges the LSN after a specified threshold or time interval.
3. Modify the StreamMessages function to implement batch processing, calling AcknowledgeLSN after a batch is completed rather than after each record.

These approaches will help reduce the WAL size by performing acknowledgments in manageable chunks, improving efficiency.

- Based on the version, conditionally execute compatible queries

title: GitHub issue olake#130: Enhance Error Execution Utilities: Add Retry, Timeout, Cancellation, and Advanced Error Handling
text:
Issue (completed): **File:** `utils/error.go`

---

### Problem

Right now, the error execution utilities (`ErrExec`, `ErrExecSequential`) work fine, but they’re missing some important features that would make them way more useful in real-world applications. Specifically, they don't support:

1. **Timeout and cancellation**: The ability to cancel or timeout functions, especially when running multiple functions at the same time.
2. **Retry Logic**: If a function fails, we can’t retry it automatically before giving up.
3. **Better Error Handling**: We need a more flexible way to handle errors, like being able to wrap errors, accumulate multiple errors, or stop execution when certain types of errors happen.

Without these features, it’s harder to handle failures, especially in complex systems or processes that involve retries, cancellations, or need better error tracking.

---

### Solution

To improve the current utilities, we could add the following features:

1. **Timeout and Cancellation Support**: Modify the existing concurrent execution function to allow cancelling or timing out tasks, so that if something goes wrong or takes too long, we can stop it early.

2. **Retry Logic**: Add a way to automatically retry failed functions a certain number of times, with some time in between, before giving up on them. This is super useful when dealing with temporary failures like network issues.

3. **Better Error Handling**: Improve the sequential execution function to allow more flexible error handl…

Issue (completed): **Overview**

This feature enables users to select specific columns from a schema during sync configuration. Only these columns are written to the destination table. It reduces cost, improves performance, simplifies downstream usage, and supports governance requirements while ensuring safe incremental and CDC-based ingestion into Apache Iceberg.

**Problem Statement**

Currently, syncs ingest all columns for a selected stream. This leads to:

- Excessive storage and compute costs for wide tables

- Increased compaction and metadata overhead

- Slower query planning and execution

- Compliance risks due to accidental ingestion of sensitive columns

As Iceberg adoption grows for CDC and streaming workloads, lack of column-level control becomes a significant scalability and governance bottleneck.

**Goals**
Enable column-level inclusion/exclusion per stream

**Non-Goals**
Column transformations (masking, hashing, renaming)

**Use Cases**

- As a data engineer, I want to ingest only required columns to reduce cost.

- As a data engineer, I want schema changes in unselected columns to not impact my sync.

- As a compliance owner, I want to ensure PII columns never reach the lake.

- As an analytics engineer, I want destination tables to remain stable and minimal.

**Proposed Solution**

## Description
Currently if we sync 10 new streams/tables in CDC mode and num_thread is configured to be 50 in config, it will create 500 go-routines for backfill. Which will have two major bad effects : 
1. Source database will be overwhelmed.
2. It will consume RAM where Olake is running.

## Steps to reproduce

Run normal sync.

## Expected behavior

Number of go-routines to spin up should be strictly controlled by the threads in config (The last thing we want is to kill the source DB).

## Actual behavior

It will spin up go-routines = num_threads (specified in config) * num of backfill tables.

Discussion:

- contributor: @shubham19may I’ll give it a try. I'm going through how the executor works, will brainstorm some ideas, and let you know about the implementation. Please unblock me if needed

- contributor: @shubham19may my thought process is to create a global buffered channel with max threads config and use it inside ConcurrentC  

this will ensure only max number of threads will be run rest of them will be blocked at a time. Am I on the right track?

go func() {
		defer close(done)
		counter := atomic.Int64{} // execution count to track the executions
		for next.Next() {
			select {
			case <-ctx.Done():
				return
			default:
				one := next.curr
				sequence := counter.Add(1)
				// schedule an execution
				globalBuffer <- struct{}{} // Acquire slot
				executor.Go(func() error {
					defer func() { <-globalBuffer }()
					return execute(ctx, one, sequence)
				})
			}
		}
	}()

So doesnt matter either its an backfill chunk query or CDC query, it should only make connection via the single concurrent function. 

But rather than creating a global channel, try to see if you can create functions of CDC & backfill and pass it to utils.concurrent menthod.

title: GitHub issue olake#87: feat: kafka source
text:
Issue (completed): ### Problem
Kafka as a source is required

Discussion:

- contributor: **Background**
Currently, OLake supports database and NoSQL sources like PostgreSQL and MongoDB for syncing data to data lakehouses. However, many modern data architectures rely on event-driven pipelines where Kafka serves as a central streaming platform for real-time data movement.

Adding Kafka as a source will allow users to ingest streaming data directly into OLake, enabling near real-time synchronization with lakehouses like Apache Iceberg

**Feature Scope**
This feature will introduce native Kafka ingestion support, enabling OLake to consume, process, and sync messages from Kafka topics efficiently. The ingestion pipeline should support:

**1. Multiple Serialization Formats**
- Avro (common for schema evolution support)
- JSON (widely used for event-driven architectures)
- Protobuf (common in gRPC and enterprise systems)
- Plain Text / CSV (for simple data streams)

**2. Schema Evolution Handling**
- Infer schema from Avro or JSON messages.
- Automatically handle new fields, type changes, and optional values.
- Provide options for strict schema enforcement or soft schema evolution.

**3. Checkpoints & Exactly-Once Processing**
- Implement offset tracking per topic & partition…

title: GitHub issue olake#86: feat: source S3
text:
Issue (completed): ## 📌 Problem

Currently, Olake **does not support reading data from S3**. Many data pipelines rely on S3 as a central source for storing structured and semi-structured data (CSV, JSON, Parquet, etc.). Lack of S3 source support limits integration capabilities for users who manage their data lakes on AWS.

## ✅ Goals

- Implement **S3 as a source connector**
- Support for various file formats (initially CSV/JSON, optionally Parquet)
- Ability to **incrementally sync new files** using metadata (e.g., timestamps, file names)
- Configurable options :
  - Bucket name
  - Path prefix
  - Region
  - File format
  - Delimiter (for CSV)
  - Compression (if any)
  - more if required

## 🛠️ Tasks

-  Define and validate config schema for S3 source  
-  Implement S3 backfill with chunking if possible
-  Add format parsers (CSV, JSON support initially)  
-  Implement incremental file discovery logic  
-  Integrate with state management to track last processed files  
-  (Optional) Add integration tests and error handling  
-  Ensure support for retry/resume and large file handling  

## 🚀Outcome

- Users can ingest datasets directly from AWS S3  
- Enables cloud-native ingestion for teams using S3 for data storage  
- Expands Olake’s use cases from s3 to datalake

Discussion:

- contributor: Hi! I'd like to contribute this S3 source connector. Here's my implementation plan:

## Proposed Approach

### Architecture
- Follow existing driver pattern (DriverInterface implementation)
- New module: `drivers/s3/`

### Key Components
1. **Config Schema**: bucket, region, prefix, credentials, file format (CSV/JSON), compression
2. **File Discovery**: List objects with prefix, track via state management
3. **Parsers**: CSV (configurable delimiter), JSON (line-delimited & array)
4. **Backfill**: Stream files in chunks, handle large files
5. **Incremental**: Track last_modified or file keys for new/updated files

### Dependencies
- AWS SDK Go v2 (already in project)
- CSV/JSON standard library parsers

### Testing
- Unit tests for parsers and config validation
- Integration tests with MinIO/LocalStack

Does this approach align with your vision? Any specific requirements or preferences before I start?

title: GitHub issue olake#46: [Proposal] Improve Parquet Writer for Better Performance and Maintainability
text:
Issue (completed): Current Implementation:
Olake currently uses the [Fraugster Parquet library](https://github.com/fraugster/parquet-go), which has the following limitations:

- Inefficient memory usage: The library consumes more memory than optimal.
- Concurrency issues: It is not well-suited for concurrent writes, limiting performance in multi-threaded environments.
- Maintenance concerns: The library is not actively maintained, which could lead to potential issues with updates or compatibility.

Proposed Improvement:
Switch to a more optimized Parquet writer that addresses these concerns, focusing on:

- Improved memory efficiency: Lower memory consumption during operations.
- Enhanced concurrency support: Better handling of concurrent writes for improved performance.
- Active maintenance: Ensuring long-term reliability and compatibility with updates.
One such library is [parquet-go](https://github.com/parquet-go/parquet-go), which is actively maintained and optimized for both memory usage and concurrency.

Benefits of the Proposal:
- Reduced resource consumption
- Improved performance in multi-threaded use cases
- Better maintainability and future-proofing of the project

title: GitHub issue olake-ui#93: Temporal Worker death results in Orphaned OLake containers
text:
Issue (completed): ## Environment

- **Deploy method**: Both docker-compose.yml and built from sources
- **Olake-UI version**:  all versions as of 20th june 2025
- **OS**: All OS
- **Cloud Provider**: All
- **Docker Params (if deployed with docker)**: N/A

## Description
When a temporal-worker crashes, the Docker container it launched (the OLake OG container) is not automatically terminated. This creates two critical problems:
 - Orphaned Containers: The original container continues to run, consuming host resources and writing data to the Iceberg tables.

 - Concurrent Execution: A Temporal retry will launch a new container for the same job, creating a race condition where two processes could be writing to the same destination, causing data duplication.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
 - `cd olake-ui`
 - `docker compose up`
 - Create a Job and run it.
 - `docker stop olake-temporal-worker`
 - `docker ps` to see that the sync container is still running. It has now become an oprhan container(process).

## Expected behavior

When the temporal worker dies, all of the ***Activities triggered by it must also stop*** and ***before stopping the activities, the last state must be saved***.

## Actual behavior

Logically on the next schedule the sync will start from the last saved state in the database which has already been synced by the orphan container resulting in data duplication.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/faec0a4e-71f0-4f98-9a49-08ef9dd53fef)

Discussion:

- contributor: <ins>**Proposed Solutions**</ins>

Here are two potential approaches to solve this problem.

**Solution A:** Save Container Labels and Cleanup

**Description:** In this approach, the worker will maintain a list of WorkflowID’s in the Postgres Database along with the container name it has spin up.

Add entry for WorkflowID and it’s corresponding ContainerID with status: "running" into the Postgres database immediately after starting the container.

Worker → PostgreSQL table:
| workflow_id | container_name | status  | created_at |
|-------------|----------------|---------|------------|
| sync-123    | olake-sync-123 | running | ...        |

The code uses dockerCmd.CombinedOutput() as stated in line 101 of file server/internal/docker/runner.go which blocks the execution i.e. does not move to next line of code unless it receives some output.

title: GitHub issue olake-ui#93: Temporal Worker death results in Orphaned OLake containers (part 2)
text:
Once the response is received from line 101 we can decide on the row entry in database based on exit code.

 - If response is success(exit status 0), delete the row with WorkflowID from the database.

 - If the response is failer(exit status >0), mark the status column for the particular WorkflowID as failed meanwhile updating the state.json file…

title: GitHub issue olake-helm#231: Worker v0.4.0 image not published to Docker Hub — S3 log storage mode non-functional with chart 0.0.30
text:
Issue (completed): ## Summary

Chart `olake-helm 0.0.30` ships S3 log file storage support and documents it as the recommended mode going forward ([install/kubernetes docs](https://olake.io/docs/install/kubernetes/)). The docs state S3 mode requires:

> OLake Version 0.12.0 and above
> OLake UI 0.7.0 and above
> Helm chart 0.0.30 and above
> **OLake worker 0.4.0 and above**

Worker v0.4.0 was tagged + GitHub-released on 2026-10-08 (release [v0.4.0](https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake-helm/releases/tag/v0.4.0), notably bundling PR #189 "chore: added-s3"). However, **no `olakego/ui-worker:v0.4.0` image exists on Docker Hub.** Only `v0.3.11` (and `:latest`, which == `v0.3.11`, pushed 2026-09-10) are available as semver tags.

Result: an operator who follows the official S3-mode setup gets a Worker that is NOT S3-aware. The symptoms are confusing and non-obvious:

1. Chart renders fine, pods come up healthy.
2. Clicking "Create Source" in the UI hangs on 4 spinning dots.
3. UI backend returns `error in request /api/v1/project/.../sources/spec: failed to get spec: failed to extract workflow response: workflow execution failed: context canceled`.
4. Temporal workflow `fetch-spec-postgres-*` reports `COMPLETED` with result `{"response":"fetch-spec-postgres-<id>/output.json"}` — a RELATIVE PATH.
5. UI tries to read that path from its own emptyDir (`/tmp/olake-config/<id>/output.json`) and fails with `no such file or directory`.
6. The spec `output.json` only exists in Worker's own pod-local filesystem…

Discussion:

- collaborator: Thanks for the report, @aanandswitch, and sorry for the trouble. The v0.4.0 release build failed, so the image was never pushed. It is now on Docker Hub (amd64 + arm64):

`olakego/ui-worker:v0.4.0` = `latest` = `sha256:1675f67c...`

To pick it up, either:
- restart the worker: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/olake-workers -n <namespace>`. This pulls the new `latest` as long as you kept the chart default `pullPolicy: Always`.
- or pin `olakeWorker.image.tag: v0.4.0` and run `helm upgrade`.

You can drop the `dev-latest` workaround. That tag tracks unreleased dev builds.

#232 fixes the release build. Let us know if S3 mode works for you on v0.4.0.

title: GitHub issue olake-helm#141: Duplicate `app.kubernetes.io/name` key in rendered labels block (v0.0.16)
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

In `olake/olake@0.0.16`, multiple templates produce a `metadata.labels` block where `app.kubernetes.io/name` appears twice. The `olake.labels` helper emits that key, and the templates themselves also hard-code a component-specific `app.kubernetes.io/name` line right before calling the helper.

Lenient YAML parsers tolerate this (last-write-wins), but strict parsers — including the YAML linter used by some CI policy-test pipelines — reject the output with `mapping key "app.kubernetes.io/name" already defined`.

A side effect even with lenient parsers: the component-specific name (e.g. `olake-ui`, `olake-shared-storage`) is silently dropped, because the helper line comes second.

## Reproduction

```bash
helm repo add olake https://datazip-inc.github.io/olake-helm
helm template test olake/olake --version 0.0.16 | grep -A 8 'name: olake-ui-config'
```

Output (truncated):
```yaml
metadata:
  name: olake-ui-config
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: olake-ui       # ← hard-coded
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: test
    app.kubernetes.io/component: olake-ui
    app.kubernetes.io/name: olake          # ← duplicate, from olake.labels helper
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm
    olake.io/part-of: olake
```

## Affected templates (v0.0.16)

```
olake/templates/olake-ui/configmap.yaml
olake/templates/olake-ui/init-user.yaml
olake/templates/olake-ui/service.yaml
olake/templates/olake-ui/ingress.yaml
olake/templates/olake-ui/deployment.yaml
olake/templates/shared-s…

Discussion:

- contributor: Hi @antoniocali thanks for the PR! Removing app.kubernetes.io/name from the helper is the right call — clean single-point fix. Will review and merge.
ETA: 2 days

title: GitHub issue olake-helm#139: Image registry prefix can't be overridden per-image (e.g. internal Harbor on host:port)
text:
Issue (completed): ## Description

The chart unconditionally prepends `olake.registryBase` (default `registry-1.docker.io`) to every user-configurable image repository. There is no way to point a single component image at a different registry, and there is no way to use a fully-qualified repository URL that includes its own host (or `host:port`).

This is the same root cause as the previously-closed #116 / #115 — re-raising because the issue is still present in `0.0.16` and bites a different setup (internal Harbor reachable on `host:port`), so I want to make sure it stays on the radar.

## Reproducer

```

Renders to:

```
image: \"registry-1.docker.io/registry.sao2.woovi.corp:8010/services/temporal-auto-setup:1.22.3\"

Setting `global.env.CONTAINER_REGISTRY_BASE` rewrites **every** image — including pinned utility images (`library/busybox:latest`, `curlimages/curl:latest`, `sig-storage/nfs-provisioner:v4.0.8`, `temporalio/ui:2.16.2`, the spark imag…
